paraphrase:
Three friends travel along the same straight road from a school to a park, each at a constant speed, and reach the park together. Alex sets off on foot first. Blair begins running one hour later, and Casey leaves by bicycle one hour after Blair. Blair’s speed exceeds Alex’s by 2 miles per hour, while Casey’s speed exceeds Blair’s by 7 miles per hour.

When the distance from the school to the park, in miles, is written as the reduced fraction \(a/b\) with positive integers \(a\) and \(b\), what is the sum of its numerator and denominator?

How many positive integers have a decimal representation containing no zeros, with digit sum thirteen, that reads identically forwards and backwards? For instance, forty-two thousand one hundred twenty-four is one such palindrome.

A horizontal disk of radius \(200\) forms the base of a solid hemisphere, also of radius \(200\), with the same center. Call a point \(X\) on the disk admissible if a ball of radius \(42\) can rest tangent to the disk at \(X\) while remaining entirely within the hemisphere. Let \(S\) be the set of admissible points.

Express the area of \(S\) as a fraction of the disk’s area in lowest terms, with positive numerator \(a\) and denominator \(b\). What is the sum of \(a\) and \(b\)?
Let \(r\) and \(s\) be distinct positive integers. How many different integers no greater than \(100\) can be expressed as \((r+1)(s+1)-1\)?

Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be points in a plane one unit apart, and let \(\alpha\) be an acute angle. First rotate \(P\) counterclockwise about \(Q\) by \(\alpha\), obtaining \(R\). Next rotate \(Q\) clockwise about \(R\) by the same angle, obtaining \(S\). The distance from \(P\) to \(S\) is four-thirds of a unit.

Express the cosine of \(\alpha\) as a reduced fraction with positive numerator \(u\) and positive denominator \(v\). What is the sum of \(u\) and \(v\)?

Consider all positive real numbers \(t\) satisfying
\[
t^{\,\log_{2026}t-20}=26^{20}.
\]
How many positive integer divisors does the product of all these values of \(t\) have?
Let \(S\) be the set of integers from \(1\) through \(6\). How many surjective functions \(f:S\to S\) return every element to itself after six successive applications?

Consider all positive integer divisors of the seventeenth power of 17017. Let \(D\) count those that are five more than a multiple of twelve. What remainder results when \(D\) is divided by one thousand?

A fair die has six initially unmarked faces. Maya has six stickers, numbered 1 through 6, and applies them in increasing numerical order. Before applying each sticker, she rolls the die and attaches that sticker to the uppermost face, covering any sticker already there.

Conditioned on the stickers numbered 2, 4, and 6 all being visible after the sixth sticker is applied, let \(q\) denote the probability that exactly five faces bear stickers. Express \(q\) as \(a/b\) in lowest terms, with \(a\) and \(b\) positive integers. What is the sum of the numerator and denominator?

Consider a triangle \(PQR\) whose sides \(PQ\), \(QR\), and \(RP\) have lengths \(13\), \(14\), and \(15\), respectively. A rotation about its circumcenter sends \(P,Q,R\) to \(U,V,W\), respectively, subject to these conditions: \(U\) and \(Q\) do not lie on the same side of the line \(VW\), and the segments \(PR\) and \(QR\) are perpendicular.

What integer is closest to the area of the hexagon with consecutive vertices \(P,U,R,W,Q,V\)?

Fill a square board with eight rows and eight columns using each integer from 1 through 64 exactly once. For every pair of cells sharing a side, take the absolute difference of their entries, and let \(T\) be the total of these differences, counting each pair once.

What remainder is obtained when the largest attainable value of \(T\) is divided by 1000?

In a plane \(\Pi\), let \(X,Y,Z\) form a right triangle with the right angle at \(X\), where \(XY\) has length \(6\) and \(XZ\) has length \(4\). Reflect the centroid of this triangle in the line through \(Y\) and \(Z\), and call its image \(W\).

Four spheres touch \(\Pi\) at \(X,Y,Z,W\), respectively, and lie on one common side of \(\Pi\). Their corresponding radii are \(1,2,3,\rho\). A second plane \(\Sigma\) is tangent to all four spheres, with all four lying on one common side of \(\Sigma\).

Express \(\rho\) as a fraction \(p/q\) in lowest terms, with \(p\) and \(q\) positive integers. What is the sum of its numerator and denominator?

For each integer \(a\) from \(0\) through \(501\), let \(T_a\) be the sum of all binomial coefficients with upper index \(10000\) whose lower indices are between \(0\) and \(10000\) and congruent to \(a\) modulo \(502\). Binomial coefficients with lower index greater than \(10000\) are taken to be zero.

How many of these \(502\) sums are divisible by the prime \(503\)?

A pentagon has all five interior angles equal. Its five diagonals have squared lengths totaling \(800\), while its five sides have squared lengths totaling \(308\). The perimeter, when squared, is \(a\sqrt{b}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers and \(b\) is squarefree. What is the sum of \(a\) and \(b\)?

Consider a square board with twice \(k\) rows and twice \(k\) columns of cells, where \(k\) is a positive integer. Choose positive integers \(r\) and \(s\), each at least two and at most twice \(k\). A rectangular cell loop of height \(r\) and width \(s\) consists of the outermost cells of an \(r\)-row, \(s\)-column rectangle. Thus it contains \(2(r+s-2)\) cells and encloses a rectangle with two fewer rows and two fewer columns, which may be empty.

For example, a board with six rows and six columns can be partitioned into four loops: a four-by-four loop in the upper-left corner, a two-by-two loop inside it, a two-row-by-four-column loop below it, and a six-row-by-two-column loop occupying the rightmost two columns.

How many partitions of a board with ten rows and ten columns into exactly five rectangular cell loops are possible, if each cell must belong to precisely one loop?
Among all arithmetic progressions consisting of integers and containing both twenty-four and thirty-four, consider those whose initial term is four. What is the sum of their tenth terms?

Ten squares are placed side by side in a single horizontal strip. Draw all their edges and, inside each square, the diagonal joining its bottom-left corner to its top-right corner.

An insect starts at the bottom-left corner of the strip, labeled \(P\), and finishes at its top-right corner, labeled \(Q\). It travels along the drawn segments between adjacent vertices. No segment may be used more than once, and every horizontal or diagonal move must go to the right; vertical moves may go either up or down.

If there are \(T\) possible routes from \(P\) to \(Q\), what is the nonnegative square root of \(T\)?

Consider a nonconvex pentagon \(PQRST\), with its vertices named in boundary order. The interior angles at \(P\) and \(T\) are right angles, while those at \(Q\) and \(S\) each measure \(45^\circ\). The vertices \(Q,R,S\) all lie in the same open half-plane bounded by the line \(PT\).

The side \(PT\) has length \(20\), the side \(QR\) has length \(\sqrt{392}\), and \(ST\) is shorter than \(PQ\). In addition, \(PQ\) has an integer length at most \(2025\), and the pentagon’s area is sixteen times an integer.

How many distinct lengths of \(PQ\) are possible?

Given a positive integer \(m\), choose a radix \(r\) that is one more than the largest digit in its decimal representation. Let \(T(m)\) be the value obtained by interpreting that same string of digits in radix \(r\).

For instance, the decimal numeral \(72\) has largest digit seven, so its chosen radix is eight. Its new value is seven times eight plus two, or \(58\).

How many positive integers smaller than \(1000\) are unchanged by this procedure?

A container holds a total of \(N\) marbles, all colored either blue or red, with no fewer than seven of either color. A sample of seven marbles is chosen uniformly at random without replacement. The chance that the sample contains three blue marbles is the same as the chance that it contains two blue marbles. What is the sum of the five smallest possible totals \(N\)?

In the \(uv\)-plane, consider the parabola
\[
v=\frac{(u-4)^2}{2}-2.
\]
Find the sum of all real values of \(\rho\) for which a circle of radius \(\rho\), with center at horizontal coordinate \(4\) and vertical coordinate \(39\), is tangent to this parabola at one or more points.

A fair six-faced die is rolled over and over. Carol receives one coin whenever the result is 5 or 6, Bob receives one coin for a 3 or 4, and Alice receives one coin for a 1 or 2.

Express the probability that both Alice and Bob have collected at least two coins before Carol gets her first coin as a reduced fraction with positive numerator \(p\) and positive denominator \(q\). What is \(q+100p\)?

Let \(PQR\) be an isosceles triangle with equal sides \(QP\) and \(QR\), and let \(J\) denote its incenter. Every side of \(PQR\) and of \(PJR\) has an integer length. The perimeter of the larger triangle is \(125/6\) times the perimeter of \(PJR\). What is the smallest possible length of \(QP\)?

Define
\[
T=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}(10^k-1)^{-1}.
\]
What remainder is obtained when the largest integer not exceeding \(100^{50}T\) is divided by \(1000\)?

In triangle \(PQR\), the sides \(PQ\) and \(PR\) have lengths \(200\) and \(225\), respectively. A point \(T\) lies on side \(QR\), and \(PT\) is the internal bisector of the angle at \(P\). A circle through \(P\) touches segment \(QR\) at \(T\), meeting segment \(PQ\) again at \(U\) and segment \(PR\) again at \(V\), with both \(U\) and \(V\) distinct from \(P\).

If the four lengths \(PU\), \(PV\), \(QT\), and \(RT\) are positive integers, determine the sum of all possible lengths of \(QR\).

Determine the largest integer \(k\) with the following property: as \((u,v,w)\) ranges over all complex triples whose squares form the roots, counted with multiplicity, of
\[
P(t)=t\bigl(t^{2}+k-11\bigr)-\frac{kt^{2}}{6}-400,
\]
the sum \(u+v+w\) takes exactly seven distinct values.

A tetrahedron has four isosceles faces, each with both equal sides of length \(\sqrt{250}\). Two faces have base length ten, while the other two have base length eighteen. Let \(O\) be the center of the sphere through all four vertices, and let \(I\) be the center of the sphere tangent to all four faces.

Express the distance between \(O\) and \(I\) as \(p/q\) in lowest terms, with \(p\) and \(q\) positive integers. What is the sum of its numerator and denominator?

Two finite subsets of the integers, \(A\) and \(B\), are called cousins when they are disjoint, have equal cardinality, and admit a bijection \(f:A\to B\) such that \(\lvert f(a)-a\rvert=1\) for every \(a\in A\). For instance, the sets \(\{4,7,8\}\) and \(\{3,6,9\}\) are cousins.

If \(A\) has precisely \(4040\) distinct cousins, what is the smallest possible cardinality of \(A\)?

Define an operation \(\star\) on integers as follows: \(x\star y\) is the sum of \(x\) and \(y\), except when \(x\) is odd and \(y\) is even, in which case it is \(x\) minus \(y\).

How many finite lists \((u_1,\ldots,u_m)\) of positive integers have total sum \(12\) and yield \(0\) when their entries are combined using \(\star\) from left to right? That is, start with \(u_1\), combine the current value with \(u_2\), then with \(u_3\), and continue through \(u_m\).

How many ordered lists \((x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_6)\), with each entry chosen from \(\{1,2,3\}\), satisfy both congruences
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{6}x_j\equiv 0\pmod 3
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sum_{j=0}^{6}x_jx_{j+1}x_{j+3}\equiv 0\pmod 3,
\]
where all subscripts are interpreted modulo \(7\)?

In the \((u,v)\)-plane, a straight line meets the curve \(v=\dfrac{u^{3}+2}{u}\), with \(u\ne 0\), at three distinct points. Two of these intersections have horizontal coordinates 6 and 7. What is the horizontal coordinate of the remaining intersection?
Among all positive multiples of \(101\) whose base-ten digits include the contiguous block \(2026\), what is the second smallest?
What is the sum of all positive integers \(m\) having at least six positive divisors for which, when those divisors are listed in decreasing order, the sixth entry is \(6\)?

Suppose \(x,y,z\) are three distinct complex numbers satisfying
\[
(y+z)^2-yz-5(y+z)=1,
\]
\[
(x+z)^2-xz-3(x+z)=0,
\]
\[
(x+y)^2-xy-3(x+y)=0.
\]
Determine the value of \(x\).

Let \(m\) be a positive integer, and let \(r\) be the integer satisfying \(r^2\le m<(r+1)^2\). What is the largest possible \(m\) such that adding \(450\) to \((r!)^{m!}\) yields an integer multiple of \(m\)?

A board initially contains each positive integer from one through 2100 exactly once. Once per second, Mark chooses two entries, removes them, and writes their greatest common divisor and their least common multiple in their place. He continues until no choice of two entries can alter the multiset on the board.

Arrange the final entries in nondecreasing order, counting repetitions. How many positive divisors does the entry in position 2026 have?

Let \(a,b,c\) be strictly positive real numbers such that
\[
(a+c)(a+b)(b+c)=40,\qquad
(b-a)(c-b)(c-a)=4,\qquad
c=\frac{3}{ab}.
\]
What is the smallest possible value of \(a\)?

Express your answer exactly using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals, without approximations or trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions.

Consider the uniquely determined integer sequence \((b_k)_{k\ge 0}\), whose terms lie in \(\{0,1,\ldots,396\}\). Its first term is \(b_0=1\), and for every \(k\ge 0\),
\[
397\mid\bigl((1+b_k)^2b_{k+1}-b_k\bigr).
\]
If \(b_{2026}=9\), what is the remainder modulo \(397\) of the sum of its first \(2027\) terms?

Find the exact value of
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{100}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
\frac{1}{2^{\left\lfloor \frac{101n}{j}\right\rfloor}},
\]
where \(\lfloor x\rfloor\) denotes the greatest integer not exceeding \(x\).

The number \(2027\) is prime. Define
\[
A=\sum_{j=0}^{2026}\frac{j\,2^j(2j)!}{(j!)^2}.
\]
What is the least nonnegative residue of \(A\) modulo \(2027\)?

An exam consists of four problems, each assigned independently and uniformly to one of four subjects: number theory, geometry, algebra, or combinatorics. You are told that geometry, algebra, and combinatorics are all represented on the exam. Under this condition, what is the probability that number theory is represented as well?

A player begins with zero points and tosses a fair four-sided die four times. Initially, the faces carry the numbers one through four. After each toss, the player earns as many points as the number currently showing, then changes that face’s number to zero for all subsequent tosses. What is the expected total number of points earned?

Arrange the integers from one through seven in a row on a blackboard. Jacob sorts the row from smallest to largest by repeatedly interchanging neighboring entries.

How many starting arrangements admit such a sorting sequence in which the entry four participates in no more than one interchange?

A unit-length rod has one end painted red. Once per minute, one of the existing pieces is selected uniformly at random and cut at its midpoint. After five such cuts, what is the expected length of the piece bearing the red mark?

Write \(N=2^9\cdot 5^9\), and let \(D\) consist of all positive divisors of \(N\). How many subsets \(A\subseteq D\) satisfy both of the following requirements?

- If an integer belongs to \(A\), then every positive divisor of that integer also belongs to \(A\).
- Whenever \(u,v\in D\) satisfy \(uv=N\), exactly one of \(u\) and \(v\) belongs to \(A\).

A borrower starts with a debt of \(\pi\) MIT, where MIT stands for Money of Indiscrete Type. Debt is measured continuously, without rounding.

Each day, a fair coin determines the repayment: one MIT for heads and two MITs for tails. If this payment leaves a balance of zero or less, the borrower is immediately declared debt-free. Otherwise, the unpaid balance is multiplied by two before the next day.

What is the probability that the borrower becomes debt-free at some finite time?

Consider a right prism with regular ten-sided bases, and denote its collection of twenty vertices by \(V\). For each plane that avoids every point of \(V\), choose either of its two open half-spaces and let \(T\) consist of the vertices lying in that half-space. How many distinct subsets \(T\) can be obtained in this way?

Tile a regular hexagon of side length four with 96 unit equilateral triangles, and denote the collection of all tiling vertices by \(V\). How many triangles of positive area whose three vertices belong to \(V\) have the hexagon’s center in their interior, rather than on their boundary?

For every positive integer \(n\), choose a finite, nonempty set \(B_n\) consisting of positive integers. Suppose that, for any positive indices \(r\) and \(s\), including equal indices, the number of elements common to \(B_r\) and \(B_s\) is the greatest common divisor of \(r\) and \(s\).

What is the smallest possible sum of the largest elements of the eight sets
\[
B_1,\quad B_2,\quad B_5,\quad B_{10},\quad B_{25},\quad B_{50},\quad B_{125},\quad B_{250},
\]
whose indices are precisely the positive divisors of \(250\)?

Consider a board whose cells are labeled by a column from \(0,1,\ldots,19\) and a row from \(0,1,2\). Count the ways to list all sixty cells, each appearing exactly once, subject to these rules:

- Each cell after the first is reached from its predecessor either by moving to an adjacent row in the same column, or by staying in the same row and advancing one column in the cyclic order \(0,1,\ldots,19,0\).
- The first cell lies in row \(2\), and the last cell lies in row \(0\).

A square \(PQRS\) has side length \(12\). A second square \(EFGH\) is positioned with \(E\) on side \(PS\) and \(F\) on side \(PQ\), while both \(G\) and \(H\) lie strictly inside \(PQRS\). The distances from \(P\) to \(E\) and \(F\) are \(4\) and \(5\), respectively. What is the area of triangle \(QRG\)?

A convex pentagon \(ABCDE\) has its vertices listed in order. The sides \(AB\) and \(DE\) have lengths \(20\) and \(26\), respectively, and the diagonal \(BD\) has length \(10\). Its interior angles at \(A\), \(C\), and \(E\) are right angles, while those at \(B\) and \(D\) are each \(135^\circ\). Find the area of the pentagon.

A rhombus \(PQRS\) of area \(120\) is inscribed in rectangle \(EFGH\), with \(P,Q,R,S\) on segments \(EF,FG,GH,HE\), respectively. The rectangle’s sides \(EF\) and \(FG\) have lengths \(12\) and \(16\). What is the length of side \(QR\)?

In a triangle \(PQR\) that is right-angled at \(P\), points \(U\) and \(V\) divide the hypotenuse \(QR\) into three consecutive pieces: \(QU\) has length \(4\), \(UV\) has length \(5\), and \(VR\) has length \(3\). A point \(S\) on the side \(PR\) is equidistant from \(P\), \(U\), and \(V\). What is their common distance from \(S\)?

Let \(\Gamma\) be a circle with center \(P\) and radius eleven. Three circles, each of radius two, are internally tangent to \(\Gamma\). Three chords of \(\Gamma\), each tangent to two of the smaller circles, form a triangle containing \(P\) in its interior. If two of these chords each have length \(\sqrt{480}\), what is the length of the remaining chord?

In triangle \(XYZ\), the side \(YZ\) has length \(8\), and \(N\) is its midpoint. Choose \(U\) on segment \(XY\) and \(V\) on segment \(XZ\) with \(XU=1\) and \(XV=3\). Each of the angles \(UNY\) and \(VNZ\) measures half the angle \(YXZ\). Find the length of \(YU\).

In an isosceles triangle \(XYZ\), the sides \(XY\) and \(XZ\) have equal length. Two interior points \(U\) and \(V\) satisfy
\[
\angle VXZ=26^\circ,\qquad \angle UXV=46^\circ,\qquad \angle YXU=20^\circ.
\]
The three segments \(YU\), \(UV\), and \(VZ\) are equal in length. What is the measure, in degrees, of \(\angle XUZ\)?

In triangle \(XYZ\), let \(T\) denote the orthocenter. Draw the internal bisector of the angle at \(X\). Its second intersections with the circles through \(X,Y,T\), through \(X,Z,T\), and through \(X,Y,Z\) are \(U,V,W\), respectively.

The four distinct points occur along the bisector in the order \(X,U,V,W\). The distances from \(X\) to \(U\) and \(V\) are \(4\) and \(5\), respectively, and the side \(YZ\) has length \(7\). What is the length of \(XW\)?

In a triangle \(PQR\), the sides \(PQ\) and \(PR\) have lengths \(5\) and \(7\), respectively. Let \(J\) be its incenter and let \(\sigma\) denote its incircle. The circle through \(Q,J,R\) meets \(\sigma\) at \(U\) and \(V\). A second circle, distinct from \(\sigma\), passes through \(U,V\), is tangent to both lines \(PQ\) and \(PR\), and has radius twice the inradius of \(PQR\). Determine the length of \(QR\).

In triangle \(PQR\), sides \(PQ\) and \(PR\) have lengths \(11\) and \(13\), respectively. Let \(M\) denote its centroid and \(U\) its circumcenter. If the orthocenter of triangle \(PMU\) lies on the line through \(Q\) and \(R\), find the length of \(QR\).

A wall is built from 2026 horizontal rows of bricks. Counting downward from the top, row \(r\) contains one fewer than the \(r\)th power of two bricks, all identical rectangles placed side by side.

A jackrabbit starts on the sole brick in the first row. At each step, it descends to a brick in the next row that shares a side with its current brick.

How many distinct sequences of steps lead the jackrabbit to the bottom row? Prove your answer.

Find all nonnegative real numbers \(r\) for which there exist complex numbers \(z\) and \(w\), each of modulus \(r\), such that
\[
(z+1)(w+1)=-99.
\]
Prove that your list is complete. Present the possible values of \(r\) as a comma-separated list inside a box.

A blackboard initially contains every integer from one through 2026, each appearing exactly once. At each step, subtract the current smallest entry from the current largest entry and use this positive result to overwrite any one entry of your choice.

What is the minimum number of steps needed for all 2026 entries to become identical? Prove that your answer is optimal.

Fix an integer \(m\ge 2\), and define, for real \(t\),
\[
G_m(t)=\frac{m-1}{m}\,\lfloor mt\rfloor
-\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}\frac{\lfloor jt\rfloor}{j},
\]
where \(\lfloor u\rfloor\) is the greatest integer not exceeding \(u\).

Determine the maximum value of \(G_m\) and all real numbers \(t\) at which it is attained.

A player is given a finite row of positive integer powers of two. A legal move replaces a pair of neighboring entries by a single power of two strictly larger than both entries removed. Play ends when the row has been reduced to one entry.

Call the sum of the initial entries \(S\). For every possible starting row, is there a sequence of legal moves whose final entry is strictly smaller than \(S+S+S+S\)?

Consider an acute scalene triangle \(PQR\), none of whose angles measures sixty degrees, and denote its circumcircle by \(\Gamma\).

Inscribe an equilateral triangle in \(\Gamma\) with \(Q\) as one vertex, and call the line joining its other two vertices \(g\). Similarly, let \(h\) be the line joining the two vertices other than \(R\) of the equilateral triangle inscribed in \(\Gamma\) that has \(R\) as a vertex.

Let \(U\) be the point where \(g\) meets the line \(PR\), and let \(V\) be the point where \(h\) meets the line \(PQ\). Take \(M\) to be the midpoint of the shorter arc from \(Q\) to \(R\) on \(\Gamma\). The lines \(g\), \(h\), and the tangent to \(\Gamma\) at \(M\) bound a triangle \(T\).

Prove that the circle through \(P,U,V\) is tangent to the incircle of \(T\).

Call a positive integer \(m\) *solitary* if it cannot be written as the sum of two nonnegative integers whose decimal representations both avoid the digit one.

How many solitary integers are strictly smaller than the 2026th power of ten? Give a proof of your answer.

Consider a triangle \(PQR\), with \(X\in QR\), \(Y\in RP\), and \(Z\in PQ\). Suppose the angles \(\angle PZY\), \(\angle QXZ\), and \(\angle RYX\) all have the same measure.

Denote the circumcenters of \(PZY\), \(QXZ\), and \(RYX\) by \(U\), \(V\), and \(W\), respectively. Let \(K\) be the circumcenter of \(PQR\), let \(L\) be the circumcenter of \(XYZ\), and let \(T\) be the circumcenter of \(UVW\).

Prove that \(T\) is equidistant from \(K\) and \(L\).
Suppose \(m,n\) are positive integers for which \(1+m^{2}+n^{2}\) is a multiple of Euler’s totient \(\varphi(1+mn)\). Prove that each of \(m\) and \(n\) occurs in the Fibonacci sequence.

Consider all connected simple graphs \(H\) with exactly thirteen vertices in which every set of four vertices contains an adjacent pair. For each such graph, write \(\kappa(H)\) for the least number of cops that can guarantee capture in the standard cops-and-robber game. What is the largest attainable value of \(\kappa(H)\)?

Consider compact complex manifolds \(Y\) of complex dimension two. For each integer \(r\) at least two, take \(r\) classes \(u_1,\ldots,u_r\) in the first cohomology of \(Y\) with real coefficients and consider their \(r\)-fold Massey product.

What is the greatest integer \(M\) for which such a product can be nonzero on at least one such manifold? Equivalently, determine the largest possible length of a nonvanishing Massey product of degree-one real cohomology classes, beyond which all such products vanish on every compact complex surface.

Consider a compact Kähler manifold \(M\) of complex dimension two, equipped with a Kähler form \(\eta\) and its induced Riemannian metric \(h\). Write \(s\) for the Chern scalar curvature, normalized by
\[
s=\tfrac12\operatorname{scal}(h),
\]
and suppose that \(s\) is strictly positive everywhere on \(M\).

Let \(a\) be the minimum value of \(s\), and define the integral two-systole by
\[
\sigma=\inf_{\substack{T\ \text{an integral two-cycle on }M\\
[T]\in H_2(M;\mathbb Z)\setminus\{0\}}}\operatorname{Mass}_{h}(T).
\]
What is the least real number \(K\), independent of \(M\) and \(\eta\), for which
\[
a\,\sigma\le K
\]
holds for every manifold and Kähler form satisfying these assumptions?

For an integer \(n\ge 2\), consider the cube
\[
Q_n=\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb R^3:0\le x_i\le n\text{ for }i=1,2,3\}.
\]
Choose three noncollinear integer-coordinate points \(v_1,v_2,v_3\) in \(Q_n\), and let their filled triangle be
\[
S=\left\{\lambda_1v_1+\lambda_2v_2+\lambda_3v_3:
\lambda_i\ge0,\ \lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=1\right\}.
\]
Also choose an integer-coordinate point \(q\) in \(Q_n\) that does not belong to \(S\). The distance from \(q\) to this triangle is the infimum, over \(y\in S\), of
\[
\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{3}(q_i-y_i)^2}.
\]

Let \(d(n)\) be the smallest such distance over all permitted choices of \(q,v_1,v_2,v_3\). Determine \(d(n)\) exactly as a function of \(n\).

Suppose \(a<b\) are primes separated by two. For each prime \(\ell\) and positive integer \(t\), write \(E_\ell(t)\) for the multiplicity of \(\ell\) in the prime factorization of \(t!\); equivalently, it is the greatest nonnegative integer \(j\) for which \(\ell^j\) divides \(t!\).

Let \(N\) be the smallest positive integer such that every integer \(t\ge N\) satisfies
\[
a^{E_a(t)}>b^{E_b(t)}.
\]
Determine \(N\) explicitly in terms of \(a\).

In six-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(\Sigma\) denote the unit five-sphere. Consider a nonminimal, totally umbilical hypersurface \(M\subset\Sigma\). After an ambient rotation, it can be described by
\[
M=\{y\in\Sigma:y_6=t\},\qquad -1<t<1,\quad t\ne0.
\]
Its induced metric is that of a round four-sphere with Euclidean radius \(r\), where
\[
r^2+t^2=1,\qquad 0<r<1.
\]

Choose stereographic conformal coordinates \(u=(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4)\) on \(M\), and prescribe the conformal factor
\[
\mu(u)=\frac{1}{1+\sum_{j=1}^{4}u_j^2}.
\]
For which value of \(r\) does there exist a biharmonic conformal immersion of this hypersurface into \(\Sigma\) with conformal factor \(\mu\)?

Choose integers \(b\) and \(m\) satisfying \(b\ge 2\) and \(b\le m\le 2(b-1)\). Consider expansions
\[
t=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} d_k b^{-k},
\qquad d_k\in\{j\in\mathbb Z:0\le j\le m\}.
\]
Within the interval from \(0\) to \(m/(b-1)\), let \(E_{b,m}\) consist of precisely those numbers \(t\) admitting one and only one such infinite digit sequence.

Determine the Hausdorff–Besicovitch dimension of \(E_{b,m}\) explicitly in terms of \(b\) and \(m\).

For a finite graph \(H\), consider a tree \(R\) with a vertex set \(A_r\subseteq V(H)\) assigned to each node \(r\) of \(R\). These sets form a tree decomposition when:
- the endpoints of each edge of \(H\) belong together to at least one \(A_r\);
- every vertex of \(H\) belongs to some \(A_r\);
- for each vertex \(x\), the nodes whose assigned sets contain \(x\) form a connected subtree of \(R\).

The width of this decomposition is one less than its largest assigned set size. Write \(\tau(H)\) for the least possible width of a tree decomposition of \(H\). Also, let \(m(x)\) count the nodes of \(R\) whose assigned sets contain \(x\), and let \(\deg_H(x)\) denote the degree of \(x\) in \(H\).

For a real parameter \(\lambda\), let \(\mathcal Q(\lambda)\) be the assertion that there is a positive constant \(K\), independent of \(H\), such that every finite graph \(H\) admits a tree decomposition with width at most \(\lambda\,\tau(H)\) and with
\[
m(x)\le K+K\deg_H(x)
\qquad\text{for every }x\in V(H).
\]

What is the greatest real number \(\beta\) such that \(\mathcal Q(\lambda)\) fails for every real \(\lambda<\beta\)?

Call the graph formed by two triangles with precisely one shared vertex a *bowtie*. For a sufficiently large integer \(N\), let \(H_{N,r}\) be constructed from a complete bipartite graph whose two part sizes are \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor\) and \(N-\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), by inserting a matching of \(r\) edges within the latter part.

Suppose \(r\) is an integer between \(2\) and \(c\sqrt N\), inclusive, where \(c>0\) is an absolute constant. Writing \(\rho(F)\) for the spectral radius of a graph \(F\), determine the minimum number of bowtie subgraphs, not required to be induced, in an \(N\)-vertex graph \(F\) subject to
\[
\rho(H_{N,r})\le \rho(F).
\]

Begin with countably infinitely many vertices and no exposed edges. Builder exposes one previously unexposed edge per turn, and Painter must immediately assign it one of two colors, red or blue.

For each integer \(m\), let \(T(m)\) be the fewest edge exposures in which Builder can guarantee, regardless of Painter’s choices, either a red three-leaf star or a blue cycle of length \(m\).

What is the total of \(T(m)\) over all integers \(m\) from fifteen through thirty, inclusive?

Consider a figure \(Q\) formed from exactly \(m\) unit lattice squares, with any two squares joined by a chain of squares sharing full edges. A hole of \(Q\) means a bounded connected component of its complement in the plane.

Restrict attention to figures for which the polygonal boundaries of distinct holes have no point in common, and no hole boundary meets the exterior boundary of \(Q\). Let \(M(m)\) denote the largest number of holes attainable by such a figure.

Determine the limiting value, as \(m\) tends to infinity, of the number of holes per square:
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty} m^{-1}M(m).
\]

Consider the complete graph \(G\) with thirty-three vertices. Draw its vertices as distinct points in the plane and its edges as simple arcs. Require that no arc contains a vertex other than its endpoints, that any pair of edges meets at only finitely many points, all of which are shared endpoints or proper crossings, and that no point is a crossing of three edges.

Restrict attention to drawings satisfying both of the following additional conditions:

- A rotation through \(120^\circ\) about a point \(C\) carries the entire drawing onto itself, permuting its vertices and edges, and \(C\) is not a vertex.
- Every edge extends to a pseudoline, and these extensions form an arrangement in which each pseudoline is a simple curve homeomorphic to the real line and each pair of pseudolines meets exactly once.

Let \(m(G)\) denote the smallest number of edge crossings in any drawing meeting all these requirements. What is the exact value of \(m(G)\)?

Consider a finite metric space \((M,\rho)\), a nonempty proper subset \(S\) of \(M\), and a Lipschitz map \(g:S\to\mathbb R\). For a real-valued function \(h\) defined on a nonempty set \(C\subseteq M\), put
\[
L_C(h)=\sup\bigl\{\rho(p,q)^{-1}|h(q)-h(p)|:\ p,q\in C,\ p\ne q\bigr\}.
\]

An extension \(h:M\to\mathbb R\) of \(g\) is called *minimal* when its Lipschitz constant on \(M\) equals that of \(g\) on \(S\).

A minimal extension \(h\) is called *absolutely minimal*, relative to the family of all subsets of \(M\setminus S\), if it is impossible to find both
- a nonempty set \(C\subseteq M\setminus S\), and
- a minimal extension \(k:M\to\mathbb R\) of \(g\)

such that \(k\) agrees with \(h\) at every point outside \(C\), while
\[
L_C(h)>L_C(k).
\]

What is the least integer \(N\) for which one can choose such a metric space with \(N\) points, such a prescribed subset \(S\), and such Lipschitz data \(g\), so that no absolutely minimal extension exists relative to the family of all subsets of \(M\setminus S\)?

Fix a prime power \(Q\), write \(\mathbb F_r\) for the prime subfield of \(\mathbb F_Q\), and let \(m>2\). In the projective space \(\mathrm{PG}(m,Q)\), denote the point set by \(X\) and the line set by \(\mathscr L\).

Form the binary matrix \(A\) with rows labeled by \(\mathscr L\) and columns labeled by \(X\), placing a one precisely when the corresponding point lies on the corresponding line. Over \(\mathbb F_r\), consider the code
\[
D_m=\bigl\{v\in\mathbb F_r^{X}:Av=0\bigr\}.
\]
Let \(\delta(m,Q)\) be the smallest number of nonzero coordinates among nonzero vectors in \(D_m\), and define \(\delta(2,Q)\) by the same construction in the projective plane over \(\mathbb F_Q\).

What is the exact formula for \(\delta(m,Q)\) in terms of \(\delta(2,Q)\), \(Q\), and \(m\)?

Let \(m\) be a positive integer that is a power of two, with \(m=1\) allowed. Consider a collection \(\mathcal A\) of bijections of the set \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) to itself. Suppose that whenever \(f\) and \(g\) are different members of \(\mathcal A\), the disjoint-cycle decomposition of \(g^{-1}\circ f\) contains a cycle whose length is divisible by two.

Determine, explicitly in terms of \(m\), the largest possible cardinality of \(\mathcal A\).

For an even integer \(\ell\ge 6\), choose an integer \(r\ge 3\) satisfying \(2r\le \ell+2\). Let \(H_d\) denote the graph of the \(d\)-dimensional cube, and let \(g(d,\ell,r)\) be the smallest number of colors in an edge-coloring of \(H_d\) for which every cycle of length \(\ell\) contains edges of at least \(r\) different colors. These cycles need not be induced subgraphs.

Suppose a particular exponent \(\beta(\ell,r)\) gives the asymptotic bound
\[
\lim_{d\to\infty}\frac{g(d,\ell,r)}{d^{\beta(\ell,r)}}=0.
\]
What is the expression for \(\beta(\ell,r)\) in terms of \(\ell\) and \(r\)?

Let \(X\) be a finite simple undirected graph. For a function \(b:V(X)\to\mathbb N\), a \(b\)-list assignment gives each vertex \(x\) a set \(A_x\) of at least \(b(x)\) available colors. A choice of colors \(\psi(x)\in A_x\) is called a proper conflict-free coloring if adjacent vertices receive different colors and, for every vertex \(x\) of positive degree, some color is used on precisely one neighbor of \(x\).

Call \(X\) proper conflict-free \((\mathrm{degree}+2)\)-choosable when such a coloring exists for every assignment of lists in which each vertex \(x\) has at least two more available colors than its degree.

Write the maximum average degree of \(X\) as
\[
\mu(X)=\max_{\substack{Y\subseteq X\\V(Y)\ne\varnothing}}
\frac{\sum_{y\in V(Y)}d_Y(y)}{|V(Y)|}.
\]

Determine the rational number \(r\) for which every connected graph \(X\) other than the cycle on five vertices is proper conflict-free \((\mathrm{degree}+2)\)-choosable whenever \(\mu(X)<r\).

Consider independent, identically distributed random bits \(Y_1,Y_2,\ldots\), each equal to one with probability \(q\) and zero with probability \(1-q\), where \(q\in(0,1)\). For any nonempty binary word \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_\ell)\), let
\[
H(a)=\inf\bigl\{k+\ell-1:\ k\ge 1,\ Y_{k+j-1}=a_j\text{ for every }j=1,\ldots,\ell\bigr\}
\]
be the index at which its first occurrence ends.

Write \(U\unlhd V\) when
\[
\mathbb P(U\le s)\ge \mathbb P(V\le s)\qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb R.
\]
Assume that the occurrence times of all nonempty finite binary words are totally ordered by this stochastic comparison: for any two such words \(a\) and \(b\), at least one of \(H(a)\unlhd H(b)\) and \(H(b)\unlhd H(a)\) holds.

What is the value of \(q\)?

For a prime power \(r\), consider the projective plane \(\Pi_r\) obtained from the vector space \((\mathbb F_r)^3\): its points correspond to one-dimensional subspaces, its lines correspond to two-dimensional subspaces, and incidence is given by containment.

Call a collection of points an *arc* when each line contains at most two points from that collection. Let \(c(r)\), the arc chromatic number of \(\Pi_r\), be the least number of pairwise disjoint arcs whose union is the entire point set.

Determine \(c(r)\) as a function of \(r\).

Call a hypergraph linear if no pair of distinct edges shares more than one vertex. Let \(Q\) be the three-uniform hypergraph consisting of five edges \(a_1,\ldots,a_5\), ordered so that consecutive edges share exactly one vertex and all nonconsecutive edges are disjoint.

For a positive integer \(m\) divisible by eleven, define \(M(m)\) as the largest number of edges in a linear three-uniform hypergraph with \(m\) vertices that has no subhypergraph isomorphic to \(Q\); the forbidden copy need not be induced. Determine \(M(m)\) as a function of \(m\).

For each positive integer \(m\), consider a path \(Q_m\) with ordered vertices \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\), in which precisely the consecutively indexed vertices are joined. Construct a graph \(H_m\) whose vertices are placements of two indistinguishable tokens on distinct vertices of \(Q_m\). Two placements are adjacent exactly when one can be obtained from the other by moving one token to a neighboring unoccupied vertex, leaving the second token in place.

Write \(d_m\) for the minimum size of a set of vertices of \(H_m\) such that every vertex outside the set has a neighbor in it. Determine
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty} m^{-2}d_m.
\]

For every positive integer \(m\), write \(S_m\) for the permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Given \(f\in S_m\), let \(J(f)\) consist of all pairs of positions \((a,b)\) with \(a<b\) for which \(f(b)<f(a)\). Equip \(S_m\) with the right weak Bruhat order, denoted by \(\leq_{\mathrm R}\), so that
\[
f\leq_{\mathrm R}g
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
J(g^{-1})\supseteq J(f^{-1}).
\]

Choose \(U_m\) and \(V_m\) independently and uniformly from \(S_m\). Assuming the following limit exists, determine its value:
\[
\ell=\lim_{m\to\infty}
\frac{\log\Pr\!\left(U_m\leq_{\mathrm R}V_m\right)}
{\log(m^m)}.
\]

For each collection \(S\) of ten distinct positive integers, let \(s(S)\) count the different sums of two members of \(S\), and let \(p(S)\) count the different products of two members. In both counts, the same member may be used twice.

What is the smallest possible value of the larger of \(s(S)\) and \(p(S)\), as \(S\) ranges over all such collections?

Consider a race with \(m\) competitors in which ties are permitted. A Fubini ranking is a list \((a_1,\ldots,a_m)\) of their ranks, with each entry an integer between \(1\) and \(m\). Every Fubini ranking is a parking function and therefore determines a unique permutation describing the cars’ final parking order.

Fix such an outcome permutation \(\sigma\), and suppose it has precisely \(r\) ascending runs, where an ascending run is a maximal consecutive block of increasing entries. What is the exact number, expressed in terms of \(m\) and \(r\), of Fubini rankings of length \(m\) whose parking outcome is \(\sigma\)?

Let \(G\) be a large random regular graph of degree \(r\), where \(r\) is an integer greater than two. For the averaging dynamics on \(G\), a finite threshold \(r_\star\) separates two regimes: above this threshold, convergence in the mean-square norm is controlled by a distinct, slower mechanism; at or below it, the dynamics exhibit a cutoff in that norm and mix just as quickly as the random walk on \(G\). What is the exact value of \(r_\star\)?

Let \(d\) be an integer at least three, and let \(\beta\) satisfy
\[
0<\beta<d,\qquad \beta>d-4.
\]
Write \(K_\beta\) for the Riesz potential of order \(\beta\). For a frequency \(\lambda>0\), consider the Choquard problem
\[
(\lambda-\Delta)v=\Phi'(v)\,[K_\beta*\Phi(v)],
\qquad v\in H^1(\mathbb R^d),
\]
with
\[
\Phi(r)=\int_0^r h(t)\,dt+|r|^{\,1+\beta/d}.
\]
Here \(h:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is continuous, has subcritical growth, and obeys
\[
r\,h(r)\geq \left(1+\frac{\beta}{d}\right)\int_0^r h(t)\,dt
\quad\text{for every }r>0.
\]
Assume also that
\[
\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{h(r)}{r^{p-1}}=1,
\qquad
1+\frac{\beta}{d}<p<\frac{d+\beta}{d-2}.
\]

Positive ground states display the following sharp transition: below a critical power \(p_{\mathrm c}\), a positive ground state exists at every positive frequency. For \(p\geq p_{\mathrm c}\), there is a number \(\lambda_p>0\) such that no positive ground state exists when \(0<\lambda<\lambda_p\), while one exists whenever \(\lambda>\lambda_p\).

Determine \(p_{\mathrm c}\) as a function of \(d\) and \(\beta\).

In the moduli space of minimal compact complex surfaces whose geometric genus and canonical self-intersection are both one, the surfaces carrying a pencil of genus-two curves constitute an irreducible subvariety. Exactly how many distinct genus-two pencils does a general member of this subvariety carry?

For the differential inclusion describing planar stationary solutions of the pressureless Euler equations, let \(q\) be the critical Lebesgue exponent separating rigidity from flexibility. For every positive \(\delta\), sequences uniformly bounded in \(L^{q+\delta}\) exhibit rigidity, whereas those uniformly bounded in \(L^{q-\delta}\) exhibit flexibility. What is the exact value of \(q\)?

Let \(H=(W,F)\) be a graph, and let a palette contain \(r\) colors. An adversary places a colored hat on each vertex, with the restriction that adjacent vertices receive different colors. Each vertex can see the hats at all adjacent vertices but cannot see its own.

Before the hats are assigned, the vertices choose deterministic rules, one per vertex, that turn the observed neighboring colors into a guess for that vertex’s own color. All guesses are made simultaneously. Call the largest integer \(r\) for which such rules guarantee at least one correct guess for every permitted hat assignment the proper-coloring hat guessing number of \(H\).

Determine this number when \(H\) is the complete graph with \(m\) vertices.

Consider a degree-two rational self-map of the projective line, defined over the rational numbers, whose automorphism group is noncommutative. What is the largest possible number of rational preperiodic points for such a map?

Suppose Popov’s method is applied with a fixed stepsize to an unconstrained pseudo-monotone variational inequality whose operator has Lipschitz constant \(K\). What is the sharp upper bound on the stepsize that guarantees convergence?

For a graph \(H\) with \(n\) vertices, call a vertex subset a general position set if no shortest path contains three of its vertices. If \(b_j\) counts such subsets with \(j\) vertices, associate to \(H\) the polynomial
\[
P_H(t)=b_0+b_1t+\cdots+b_nt^n.
\]

Consider complete multipartite graphs whose \(q\) vertex classes all have the same size \(s\). There is a largest positive integer \(M\) such that, for every integer \(q\ge 2\) and every integer \(s\) between \(1\) and \(M\), the polynomial \(P_H(t)\) is both log-concave and unimodal. Determine \(M\).

For each integer \(m\) greater than one, take the digit set
\[
A_m=\{j\in\mathbb Z:|j|<m\}.
\]
Define \(E_m\) to consist of all complex numbers \(z\) with \(|z|>1\) for which some sequence \((a_r)_{r\ge1}\) drawn from \(A_m\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_r}{z^r}=-1.
\]
Also define
\[
L_m=\left\{z\in\mathbb C:\ |z|>1,\quad
\max\bigl\{|1+z|^2,\ |1-z|^2\bigr\}<2m\right\}.
\]
Determine the least integer \(m\) greater than one for which every nonreal element of \(E_m\) belongs to \(L_m\).

For each integer \(m\ge 2\), choose independently two permutations \(a\) and \(b\) of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Let \(b\) be uniform among all permutations, and let \(a\) be uniform among the nonidentity permutations whose square is the identity. As \(m\) tends to infinity, what is the limiting probability that \(a\) and \(b\) together generate every permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\)?

Suppose \(\mathscr D\) is a small stable \(\infty\)-category equipped with a bounded \(t\)-structure, and write \(\mathscr A\) for its heart. Fix an integer \(r\geq 1\), and assume that the realization functor gives isomorphisms on Ext groups in every degree at most \(r\) for each pair of objects of \(\mathscr A\). As a function of \(r\), what is the least integer \(q\) for which the map from \(K_q(\mathscr A)\) to \(K_q(\mathscr D)\) induced by inclusion of the heart is necessarily an isomorphism?

Consider the one-space-dimensional Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation with flat initial data, and denote its solution by \(H(s,y)\). Write \(U(s,y)\) for the solution of the associated stochastic heat equation, also with flat initial data. Let \(K\) be the square of the expected reciprocal of \(U(s,0)\).

For fixed time \(s\), determine, in terms of \(K\) and \(s\),
\[
\lim_{|y|\to\infty}
y^{2}\exp\!\left(\frac{y^{2}}{4s}\right)
\operatorname{Cov}\!\bigl(H(s,0),H(s,y)\bigr).
\]

Find the exact value of
\[
\int_0^1
\frac{\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{t^2+2}}{\sqrt{t^2+4}}\right)}
{\sqrt{t^2+2}\,(t^2+1)}\,dt.
\]
In combinatorial game theory, determine the sum of all positive integers that never occur as the number of elements of a finite partisan misère quotient.

For graphs \(A\) and \(B\), write \(\rho(A,B)\) for the smallest number of vertices in a host graph such that every red–blue coloring of its edges contains either an induced copy of \(A\) with all edges red or an induced copy of \(B\) with all edges blue.

Let \(S\) be the three-vertex path. For an integer \(m\) at least two, construct \(T_m\) from \(m\) vertex-disjoint edges by adding one new vertex joined to every endpoint, with no other edges added.

Determine \(\rho(S,T_m)\) exactly in terms of \(m\).

For each prime power \(Q\), choose a \(d\)-dimensional subspace \(V\) of \(\mathbb{F}_Q^{\,m}\) uniformly from all such subspaces. Let \(Q\), \(m\), and \(d\) all tend to infinity, with
\[
\frac{d}{m}\longrightarrow 0,
\qquad
\frac{m!}{Q\,d!\,(m-d)!}\longrightarrow \theta,
\]
where \(\theta\) is a fixed positive finite constant. What is the limiting probability that the linear code \(V\) is maximum distance separable (MDS)?

Let \(m\) be an integer with \(m\ge 2\), and consider the generalized Benjamin–Bona–Mahony evolution
\[
\partial_\tau v-\partial_y^2\partial_\tau v
=-\partial_y\!\left(v^m+v\right),
\]
where the spatial domain is either the real line or the one-dimensional torus.

Denote its sharp Sobolev threshold by \(\sigma_*(m)\). At every regularity \(\sigma\) at or above this threshold, the initial-value problem is unconditionally locally well-posed in
\[
C\bigl([0,L];H^\sigma\bigr),
\]
with no auxiliary function-space requirements. Below the threshold, any flow map that is defined and continuous on an \(H^\sigma\)-neighborhood of zero, taking values in this same solution space, fails to be \(m\)-times continuously Fréchet differentiable at zero.

Determine \(\sigma_*(m)\) in terms of \(m\).

Define the Takagi map \(F:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}\) by
\[
F(u)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{1-k}\,\operatorname{dist}\!\left(2^{k-1}u,\mathbb{Z}\right),
\]
where \(\operatorname{dist}(v,\mathbb{Z})\) is the distance from \(v\) to the nearest integer.

Starting from \(u_0=a\) in the unit interval, form the sequence \(u_{j+1}=F(u_j)\). What value does \(u_j\) approach as \(j\to\infty\) for Lebesgue-almost every starting point \(a\)?

Suppose \(Y\) is an aspherical 3-manifold with the same integral homology as the 3-sphere. Let \(p\colon X\to Y\) be a finite-sheeted regular covering, and suppose that \(X\) has positive first Betti number. What is the sharp lower bound for the first Betti number of \(X\)?

Apply the unmodified Cauchy combination test to \(n\) p-values generated by a standard single-factor Gaussian copula with equal pairwise correlation \(r_n>0\), where \(r_n\) tends to zero as \(n\) grows. For a fixed significance threshold \(q\) strictly between zero and one-half, the test is asymptotically exact if and only if
\[
r_n=o\!\left((\log n)^{-\beta}\right).
\]
What is the exact value of \(\beta\)?

For each positive integer \(m\), write \(\mathfrak S_m\) for the permutation group on \(m\) letters and \(\mathcal X_m\) for its irreducible complex characters. Consider three sequences of conjugacy classes \(D_m,E_m,F_m\) in \(\mathfrak S_m\).

Fix a real number \(h>0\). As \(m\) tends to infinity, suppose that each of \(D_m\) and \(E_m\) has exactly the greatest integer not exceeding \(h\sqrt m\) fixed points. Suppose also that, for a sufficiently large constant \(q>0\) depending on \(h\), every cycle of length greater than one in any of the three classes has length at least \(q(\log m)\sqrt m\). Finally, require
\[
\operatorname{sgn}(F_m)=\operatorname{sgn}(D_m)\operatorname{sgn}(E_m).
\]

If \(e_m\) denotes the identity permutation, determine
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty}
\sum_{\psi\in\mathcal X_m}
\psi(D_m)\psi(E_m)\,\frac{\psi(F_m)}{\psi(e_m)},
\]
the limiting character sum in the Frobenius formula.
Consider the reciprocals of the factorials of all positive integers. Find the sum of the distinct values among them that belong to the standard middle-thirds Cantor set.

For a finite simple undirected graph \(H\), give each vertex \(x\) a set \(A_x\) of exactly \(r\) colors. A packing for these lists consists of \(r\) proper vertex colorings \(c_1,\ldots,c_r\) such that, at every vertex \(x\), the colors \(c_j(x)\), as \(j\) ranges from \(1\) to \(r\), use each element of \(A_x\) exactly once.

Call \(H\) list \(r\)-packable if such a packing exists for every choice of the sets \(A_x\). Write \(p(H)\) for the least integer \(r\) for which this property holds. For each tree-width bound \(b\), let \(M(b)\) denote the maximum of \(p(H)\) over all finite simple undirected graphs \(H\) whose tree-width is no greater than \(b\).

Determine the exact value of \(M(3)\).

Suppose a finite tree \(G\) has \(m\) leaves and maximum vertex degree \(\Delta\), where \(\Delta\) is at least two. Use the leaves as the boundary, and denote the smallest positive Steklov eigenvalue by \(\sigma\). What is the sharp upper bound for \(\sigma\) in terms of \(\Delta\) and \(m\), with equality if and only if \(G\) is a star?

In Bayesian learning theory for neural networks, the Local Learning Coefficient (LLC) measures effective model complexity. Suppose a linear layer with parameter matrix \(A\) has \(q\) output coordinates and is fitted under squared-error loss to a realizable teacher, with a nondegenerate input distribution before normalization.

RMSNorm places the inputs on a sphere and, because this surface has nonzero curvature, leaves the LLC of \(A\) unchanged. LayerNorm, by contrast, subtracts the coordinate mean, restricting the inputs to a flat linear hyperplane containing the origin.

Relative to RMSNorm, what is the exact decrease in the LLC of \(A\) caused by this mean-centering constraint in LayerNorm?

Suppose \(U\) is a smooth complex quasi-projective surface whose logarithmic Kodaira dimension is nonnegative, and let \((Y,B)\) be a compactification. Write
\[
p=\dim_{\mathbb C}H^0\!\left(Y,\mathcal O_Y(K_Y+B)\right),
\qquad
r=\dim_{\mathbb C}H^0\!\left(Y,\Omega_Y^1(\log B)\right).
\]
Assume that \(U\) fails to have maximal Albanese dimension. The sharp lower bound for its first logarithmic plurigenus \(p\), expressed in terms of its logarithmic irregularity \(r\), is a linear polynomial \(L\) satisfying
\[
L(r)\le p.
\]
What is \(L(r)\)?

Consider a family \(\mathcal F\) of projective subspaces of dimension \(d-1\) in a projective space of dimension \(rd-1\) over the field with \(s\) elements. Suppose no hyperplane contains more than \(m\) members of \(\mathcal F\), and the family meets the upper bound, so that
\[
\#\mathcal F-m=s^d(m+2-r).
\]
When \(r=4\) and \(s>2\), such a family can exist only for one particular value of \(m\). What is that value in terms of \(s\) and \(d\)?

Place \(n\) ordered points in the interval from zero to one so as to minimize their energy under the bounded pair interaction
\[
V_\alpha(s)=\frac{1}{\exp(s^\alpha)},\qquad \alpha>0,
\]
where \(s\) denotes the distance between two points. In the regime \(\alpha>1\), write \(\alpha_n^\ast\) for the critical exponent above which interior points cease to be optimal. When \(n\) is odd—twice an integer \(r\) plus one—this threshold has an exact universal value. What is \(\alpha_{2r+1}^\ast\)?

For the massive Thirring model, let the rational-solution hierarchy be generated by double-Wronskian determinants. Its member of order \(m\) represents a nonlinear superposition of \(m\) equal-mass algebraic solitons and is associated with an embedded eigenvalue whose algebraic multiplicity is \(m\). Suppose the leading-order polynomials each have precisely \(m\) real zeros. In the limit of large absolute time \(|\tau|\), how many poles does this order-\(m\) solution have in the upper half of the complex spatial \(\zeta\)-plane, expressed as a function of \(m\)?

Let \(r\) and \(s\) be integers, each at least two. Define \(P(r,s)\) to be the largest possible product of the numbers of edges in two hypergraphs \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal B\) satisfying the following conditions:

- Every edge of \(\mathcal A\) meets every edge of \(\mathcal B\).
- The edges of \(\mathcal A\) all have size \(r\), and its minimum vertex cover has size \(s\).
- The edges of \(\mathcal B\) all have size \(s\), and its minimum vertex cover has size \(r\).

Determine \(P(r,r)\) exactly in terms of \(r\), for all sufficiently large \(r\).

For a graph \(H\), let \(D(H)\) be the largest number of classes in a partition of its vertex set such that every class is a dominating set. Consider all cographs—that is, graphs with no induced path on four vertices—and write \(m\) for their minimum degree. Suppose the sharpest universal affine lower bound for this family is
\[
D(H)\ge \beta+\alpha m,
\]
where \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R\). Determine the ordered pair \((\alpha,\beta)\).

Fix a prime power \(q\ge 3\). Let \(H\) be the complete bipartite graph with \(q\) vertices in each part, and let \(F\) be the complete bipartite graph whose parts have sizes \(2\) and \(q+1\).

Write \(M_q(N)\) for the largest number of copies of \(H\) in an \(N\)-vertex graph containing no copy of \(F\). For each positive integer \(j\), set \(N_j=q^{2j}/q\). Determine
\[
\lim_{j\to\infty} N_j^{-2}M_q(N_j).
\]

Given a graph \(X\) and a nonnegative integer \(r\), let \(\mathcal R_r(X)\) be the graph whose vertices are the independent subsets of \(V(X)\) of size \(r\). Two such subsets are adjacent precisely when one is obtained from the other by moving a single token to a neighboring vertex of \(X\), with the resulting set remaining independent.

Call a graph realizable with \(r\) tokens if it is isomorphic to \(\mathcal R_r(X)\) for some graph \(X\). Among integers \(r\) at least two, what is the smallest for which the \(3\)-by-\(3\) grid—the Cartesian product of two three-vertex paths—is realizable with \(r\) tokens?

For a knotted surface in the four-sphere, define its tri-plane crossing number by minimizing the number of crossings over all tri-plane diagrams representing bridge trisections of that surface. Determine this invariant exactly for the trefoil’s 2-twist spin.

Place pebbles on the vertices of a digraph \(G\). A legal move consists of taking two pebbles from a vertex \(x\) and adding one pebble to a vertex \(y\), provided there is an arc directed from \(x\) to \(y\).

Define \(s(G)\) to be the smallest integer at least two for which every placement of that many pebbles can, after finitely many legal moves, have all surviving pebbles gathered at one vertex.

For each integer \(m\) at least two, let \(Z_m\) be the cycle on \(m\) vertices with all arcs oriented cyclically. Determine an exact expression for \(s(Z_m)\) in terms of \(m\).

Consider a fixed infinite rooted tree formed from a ray \(v_0,v_1,v_2,\ldots\), rooted at \(v_0\). For each integer \(m\geq 1\), attach to \(v_m\) a separate finite path of exactly \(m\) edges, with no other vertices or edges added.

Fix a bias parameter \(\rho\in(0,1)\). A random walk \((Y_t)_{t\geq0}\) starts at \(v_0\). At any vertex other than the root that has \(d\) children, it chooses its parent with probability \(\rho/(d+\rho)\) and each individual child with probability \(1/(d+\rho)\). At the root, its next step is to \(v_1\) with certainty.

Call a positive integer \(s\) a cut time when no vertex visited before step \(s\) is visited at step \(s\) or at any later step. Let \(C(n)\) count the cut times among steps \(1,\ldots,n\).

What is the almost sure value of
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{C(n)}{\ln n}\,?
\]

Determine the least real threshold \(t\) such that, for any trivially perfect graph \(H\), every eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix lying between \(t\) and zero, inclusive, is either negative one or zero.

Let \(H\) be a connected graph with \(N\) vertices. For each vertex \(v\), define its transmission by
\[
t(v)=\sum_{u\ne v} d_H(u,v).
\]
The distance Laplacian \(L_{\mathrm{dist}}(H)\) has diagonal entry \(t(v)\) at vertex \(v\) and off-diagonal entry \(-d_H(u,v)\) at distinct vertices \(u,v\). Write its eigenvalues in decreasing order as
\[
\lambda_1(H)\ge\lambda_2(H)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_N(H),
\]
and denote by \(\mathcal W(H)\) the Wiener index, the sum of distances over all unordered pairs of distinct vertices.

The distance-Laplacian version of Brouwer’s conjecture asserts that, for every integer \(k\) from \(1\) through \(N\),
\[
\lambda_1(H)+\cdots+\lambda_k(H)
\le \mathcal W(H)+\frac{k(k+1)(k+2)}{6}.
\]

For connected graphs of diameter two, this bound is known to hold except for precisely two graph–integer pairs. One is the star with three leaves when \(k=2\). The other is a star with \(s\) leaves when \(k=k_*\). Determine \(s+k_*\).

Let \(F\) be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let \(Z\) be a reduced collection of eleven points in generic position in the projective plane over \(F\). Write \(J\) for its defining ideal. Define the relation type \(\rho(Z)\) as the largest degree, measured in the presentation variables of the Rees algebra of \(J\), among the minimal generators of that algebra’s defining ideal. What is \(\rho(Z)\)?

For an integer \(r>4\), apply West’s stack-sorting map \(r-4\) times to every permutation of length \(2(r-2)\). Let \(N_r\) be the number of distinct permutations obtained, and write \(\operatorname{Bell}(r)\) for the Bell number with index \(r\). What is an explicit formula in \(r\) for
\[
N_r-\operatorname{Bell}(r)?
\]

Write \(H(r,s;N)\) for the largest possible number of empty convex polygons with \(r\) vertices determined by \(N\) planar points in general position, subject to the condition that no empty convex polygon with \(s\) vertices occurs.

Suppose \(r\) and \(b\) are positive integers satisfying \(2b+2\le r\). Among configurations of \(r+b\) points containing no empty convex polygon with \(r+1\) vertices, what is the exact maximum number of empty convex polygons with \(r\) vertices, expressed as a function of \(b\)?

Fix an integer \(n>1\), and equip the integer lattice \(\mathbb Z^n\) with the coordinatewise partial order. For a pair of lattice points, form a new point by choosing the smaller entry in each coordinate.

As a function of \(n\), determine the supremum of all real numbers \(s\) with the following property: there is a positive constant \(C_n\), depending only on \(n\), such that every finite antichain \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) produces at least \(C_n(\#S)^s\) different points by applying this operation to pairs of its members.

Let \(q\) be a real number greater than \(1\) and at most \(2\). For a graph \(H\), define
\[
h_q(H):=\max_{\substack{T\subseteq V(H)\\T\ne\emptyset}}
\bigl(|E(H[T])|\,|T|^{-q}\bigr),
\]
where \(H[T]\) is the subgraph induced by \(T\).

The sharp asymptotic estimate for the adjacency spectral radius \(\rho(H)\), expressed in terms of \(h_q(H)\) and the number of vertices, changes behavior when \(q=\tfrac32\). At this critical value, every graph \(H\) on \(N\) vertices having at least one edge satisfies
\[
\frac{\rho(H)}{h_{3/2}(H)\,(N\log N)^{1/2}}
\le K+o(1)
\qquad\text{as }N\to\infty,
\]
with the error term tending to zero in that limit.

What is the exact smallest possible value of \(K\)?

Fix a positive integer \(d\) and a parameter \(r\) satisfying \(\tfrac12<r<1\). Write \(G=(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^d\), with its uniform probability distribution. For real-valued functions \(u,v\) on \(G\), use the notation
\[
(u,v)_G=2^{-d}\sum_{a\in G}u(a)v(a),
\qquad
|u|_{2,G}^{\,2}=2^{-d}\sum_{a\in G}u(a)^2,
\]
and define their normalized convolution by
\[
(u\star v)(a)=2^{-d}\sum_{b\in G}v(a+b)u(b),
\]
where addition is coordinatewise modulo two.

Let \(N_r\) denote the usual Bonami–Beckner noise operator: \(N_rv(a)\) is the expected value of \(v\) after each coordinate of \(a\) is independently flipped with probability \((1-r)/2\).

Determine the largest constant \(C_{r,d}\), depending only on \(r\) and \(d\), for which
\[
C_{r,d}\,|u\star v|_{2,G}^{\,2}\le (u,N_rv)_G
\]
for every pair of functions \(u,v:G\to[0,1]\).

For a graph \(J\), write \(M_J(v)\) for the largest number of subgraphs isomorphic to \(J\) that can occur in a planar graph with \(v\) vertices; these subgraphs need not be induced. Let \(T\) be the graph formed from a triangle by adding a fourth vertex adjacent to exactly one vertex of the triangle.

Determine \(M_T(v)\) exactly as a function of \(v\), for every integer \(v\) at least four.

Write \(C_t\) for the complete graph with \(t\) vertices. Fix integers \(t\ge 3\) and \(m>t-1\). Among graphs on \(N\) vertices whose largest matching has exactly \(m\) edges, consider those that contain no subgraph isomorphic to \(C_t\), but acquire such a subgraph whenever an edge is added between two nonadjacent vertices.

For all sufficiently large \(N\), what is the smallest possible edge count of such a graph?

Call a spanning tree a HIST (homeomorphically irreducible spanning tree) if every vertex has degree either one or at least three in the tree. Given an integer \(m\) with \(13\le m\), determine the largest possible edge count of a simple, 2-connected graph on \(m\) vertices that admits no HIST.

Let \(d\) and \(k\) be integers satisfying \(d\geq 6\), \(d\leq k\), and \(k+3\leq 2d\), with \(k\) and \(d\) of the same parity.

Call an edge cut essential when deleting its edges leaves at least two components, each containing more than one vertex. The essential edge-connectivity is the smallest size of such a cut. Define the adjacency spectral gap to be the largest adjacency eigenvalue minus the second largest.

In terms of \(d\) and \(k\), what is the greatest possible adjacency spectral gap of a connected \(d\)-regular graph whose essential edge-connectivity does not exceed \(k\)?

Consider a triangle-free graph \(H\) on \(m\) vertices whose edges have been assigned colors. For each vertex \(x\), let \(c_H(x)\) count the distinct colors appearing on edges incident with \(x\), and denote the smallest such count by
\[
\mu(H):=\min_{x\in V(H)}c_H(x).
\]
Suppose that, for all sufficiently large integers \(m\), the condition \(\mu(H)\geq T(m)\) guarantees a four-edge cycle whose edges have pairwise distinct colors. If this threshold is best possible and has the form
\[
T(m)=\frac{m}{q}+\frac{p}{q},
\qquad p,q\in\mathbb Z,\quad q\ne0,
\]
what is the exact formula for \(T(m)\)?

For Berry’s random wave model on Euclidean space of integer dimension \(n\) at least two, fix a positive excursion threshold \(t\). The large-scale spatial fluctuations of the excursion volumes are known to converge, in the dual of the Schwartz space on \(\mathbb R^n\), to a fractional Gaussian field obtained by applying the inverse \(\beta\)-th power of the negative Laplacian to standard Gaussian white noise in that dimension. What is the exact value of \(\beta\)?

For a graph \(F\), let \(s(F)\) denote the smallest number of edges in a maximal matching. Define its harmonic index \(h(F)\) by assigning each edge joining vertices \(x\) and \(y\) the weight
\[
\left(\frac{\deg_F(x)+\deg_F(y)}{2}\right)^{-1}
\]
and summing these weights over all edges.

Among all trees \(R\) containing at least one edge, let \(a\) be the infimum of \(s(R)\,h(R)^{-1}\), and let \(b\) be its supremum. Determine the ordered pair \((a,b)\).

Consider a tripartite hypergraph \(G\) in which every edge has three vertices and each vertex class has cardinality \(m\). For each vertex \(x\), form a graph \(L_x\) on all vertices other than \(x\), joining \(y\) to \(z\) precisely when \(\{x,y,z\}\) is an edge of \(G\). Write \(\lambda_x\) for the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of \(L_x\).

Determine the exact sharp constant \(\gamma\) with the following property: for every positive \(\varepsilon\), there is an integer \(M\) such that, whenever \(m\ge M\) and
\[
\min_{x\in V(G)}\frac{\lambda_x}{m}>\gamma+\varepsilon,
\]
the hypergraph \(G\) has a perfect matching. Here sharpness means that no smaller constant can replace \(\gamma\) in this assertion.

Let \(T\) be an infinite tree in which every vertex has exactly \(k\) neighbors, with \(k>2\). Place one active player at each vertex. Every edge carries an independent Poisson clock, all with the same rate. When a clock rings and both endpoint players are still active, a fair coin determines which player survives; the other is removed permanently. Rings on edges with an inactive endpoint have no effect.

In the limiting configuration, no edge joins two active players. What is the expected proportion of players that survive, or equivalently, the probability that the player at a fixed vertex survives forever?

Over the complex numbers, consider a general hypersurface \(Y\) of weighted degree ten in the weighted projective three-space with coordinate weights one, two, three, and five. This is a log del Pezzo surface, and each of its singularities is a cyclic quotient singularity given by a group of order three acting on two coordinates with weights one and one. Denote its associated canonical smooth Deligne–Mumford stack by \(\mathfrak{Y}\).

How many objects constitute a full exceptional collection in the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on \(\mathfrak{Y}\)?

Determine the number of ordered triples \((r,s,n)\) of nonnegative integers such that the absolute difference between \(n^2\) and \(3^s2^r\) is at least one but strictly less than three times the larger of \(r\) and \(s\).

Fix an odd prime \(q\) and an integer \(m\) greater than one, and let \(C\) be cyclic with \(q^{m}\) elements. Among the subgroups \(K\) of \(\operatorname{Aut}(C)\), exactly three have the property that the Schur ring defined by their orbits yields an almost commutative Terwilliger algebra. What is the sum of the distinct subgroup orders that occur for these choices of \(K\)?

Let \(a,b,c\) be positive integers with \(b>a\). Consider graphs in which every pair of disjoint vertex sets, each of cardinality \(a\), has at least one edge joining the two sets.

Define \(M_a(b,c)\) to be the least integer \(n\) such that, for every such graph on \(n\) vertices, every assignment of \(c\) colours to its edges produces \(b\) pairwise vertex-disjoint edges all of the same colour.

Determine an exact closed-form expression for \(M_a(b,c)\) in terms of \(a,b,c\).

Determine the least real constant \(\gamma\) with the following property: for every sequence \((H_m)\) in which \(H_m\) has exactly \(m\) vertices, contains no complete subgraph on five vertices, and has largest independent set of size \(a_m\) satisfying \(a_m/m\to 0\), one can make \(H_m\) bipartite by deleting at most
\[
(\gamma+\varepsilon_m)m^2
\]
edges, where \(\varepsilon_m\to 0\) and the sequence \((\varepsilon_m)\) may depend on the chosen graph sequence.

Consider a vector-valued fractional Brownian motion \(B\) with Hurst index \(h\), where \(0<h\leq \tfrac12\). Among its local rough-path lifts that are square-integrable, restrict attention to those whose laws are invariant under coordinate permutations, time shifts, and scaling.

For almost every Hurst index greater than one quarter, these requirements single out the canonical lift. Yet precisely one index in the stated range admits a one-parameter family of lifts with all these properties. Which Hurst index is it?

For a positive integer \(m\), consider all real square matrices \(A\) of order \(m\) whose entries are nonnegative, whose rows each sum to one, and whose entries vanish whenever the row and column indices differ by more than one. In terms of \(m\), what is the largest possible number of eigenvalues of \(A\) that are strictly less than zero, counted according to algebraic multiplicity?

Let \(H\) be a graph. A vertex subset \(A\) is said to isolate \(H\) when deleting \(A\) together with all vertices adjacent to members of \(A\) leaves a graph with no edges. Write \(j(H)\) for the smallest size of such a subset.

Define \(q(H)\) to be the least number of distinct edges that must each be subdivided once so that the resulting graph has isolation number larger than \(j(H)\).

Among all trees \(R\) that are not stars, what is the largest possible value of \(q(R)\)?

For a group \(H\), let \(Q(H)\) denote its conjugacy quandle: its underlying set is \(H\), and the product \(a*b\) is obtained by conjugating \(a\) by \(b\), namely \(b^{-1}(ab)\).

Recall that finite groups \(H\) and \(K\) are isoclinic when there are isomorphisms
\[
\phi:H/Z(H)\longrightarrow K/Z(K),
\qquad
\psi:H^{\mathrm{der}}\longrightarrow K^{\mathrm{der}},
\]
where \(H^{\mathrm{der}}\) and \(K^{\mathrm{der}}\) are their commutator subgroups, with the following compatibility: for every pair \(a,b\in H\), the map \(\psi\) sends their commutator to the commutator of any representatives in \(K\) of the cosets \(\phi(aZ(H))\) and \(\phi(bZ(H))\), respectively.

What is the smallest positive integer \(m\) for which two groups, each having \(m\) elements, are not isoclinic but have isomorphic conjugacy quandles?

For a finite group \(F\), form a graph \(\mathcal C_F\) whose vertices are the subgroups other than the identity subgroup and \(F\) itself. Join distinct vertices \(A\) and \(B\) precisely when every element of \(F\) can be written as \(ab\), with \(a\in A\) and \(b\in B\). Delete every isolated vertex to obtain a graph \(\mathcal D_F\).

As \(F\) ranges over all finite groups for which \(\mathcal D_F\) has a cycle, collect the distinct possible lengths of its shortest cycle into a set \(T\). What is the sum of the numbers in \(T\)?

Write \(G_k\) for the Fibonacci sequence, whose first two terms are both \(1\). For each positive integer \(r\), let \(C(r)\) count the nonempty subsets of the integers from \(1\) through \(r\) whose elements have a greatest common divisor coprime to \(r\).

Consider every ordered pair of positive integers \((k,r)\) for which \(C(r)=G_k\). What is the sum of the products \(kr\) over all such pairs?

Consider zero together with all odd prime numbers. Let \(T\) consist of those numbers \(c\) in this collection for which there is an algebraically closed field \(F\) of characteristic \(c\) and a rational elliptic or quasi-elliptic surface over \(F\) that is not a Jacobian surface and has a nonzero global vector field.

What is the sum of all the numbers in \(T\)?

Fix a prime \(p\). For each odd prime power \(r\), consider the group \(H_r\) of invertible \(2\times2\) matrices over the field with \(r\) elements. Write \(A_p(r)\) for the number of entries in its complex character table that do not belong to \(p\overline{\mathbb Z}\), where \(\overline{\mathbb Z}\) is the ring of all algebraic integers.

There is a constant \(C\) such that, for every positive \(\delta\),
\[
A_p(r)-Cr^4=O_\delta\!\left(r^{3+\delta}\right)
\]
as \(r\) tends to infinity through odd prime powers. Determine \(C\) exactly.

Fix integers \(r\) and \(m\), where \(r\) is at least ten and \(m\geq 2(r+1)\). Call a simple graph \(H\) saturated for this property if no subgraph of \(H\) has a collection of \(r+1\) pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees, but inserting an edge between any two nonadjacent vertices creates a subgraph with such a collection.

Among all graphs on \(m\) vertices that are saturated in this sense, what is the largest possible number of edges?

Let \(k\) be an integer at least fifty. Among all finite partially ordered sets whose automorphism group is isomorphic to the direct product of a cyclic group of order two and a cyclic group of order \(2^k\), what is the smallest possible number of elements, expressed as a function of \(k\)?

Let a branching random walk on the real line have offspring probabilities \((q_j)_{j\ge 0}\). Its expected number of children is
\[
\mu=\sum_{j\ge 1}j q_j,\qquad 0<\mu<1.
\]
Suppose the displacement \(Y\) is independent of the number of children and has finite second moment. For a slowly varying function \(L\), constants \(c>0\), \(0<\beta<1\), and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), assume its right tail satisfies
\[
\mathbb P\{Y>t\}=\frac{L(t)t^\alpha}{\exp(c\,t^\beta)}.
\]

Write \(R_r\) for the rightmost position occupied by a particle in generation \(r\), and set \(R_*=\sup_{r\in\mathbb N}R_r\). Determine, in terms of \(q_0\) and \(\mu\), the exact value of
\[
\lim_{t\to+\infty}
\frac{\mathbb P\{R_*>t\}}{L(t)t^\alpha\exp(-c\,t^\beta)}.
\]

Let \(m\) be an integer greater than \(1\), and let \(H\) be a graph whose number of edges is divisible by \(m\). Define \(\rho_m(H)\) to be the smallest order of a complete graph for which every assignment of residues modulo \(m\) to its edges produces a copy of \(H\) with edge labels adding to a multiple of \(m\).

Write \(B_{a,b}\) for the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes \(a\) and \(b\). For every integer \(r>2\), the number \(\rho_3(B_{r,3})\) exceeds \(r\) by three, apart from finitely many exceptional choices of \(r\), for which it exceeds \(r\) by four.

What is the sum of all these exceptional integers \(r\)?

Given a finite abelian group \(A\) and a graph \(H\), let \(T(H,A)\) be the largest possible size of a subset \(D\) of the nonidentity elements of \(A\) such that \(D\) is closed under taking additive inverses and the Cayley graph with vertex set \(A\), where distinct \(x,y\) are adjacent exactly when \(y-x\in D\), contains no copy of \(H\).

Let \(q\) be any odd prime, and let \(t\) be an integer satisfying \(0<t<q\). What is the exact value of \(T(K_{t+1},\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z)\), where \(K_{t+1}\) is the complete graph with \(t+1\) vertices?
Determine the number of isomorphism classes of skew left braces with additive group isomorphic to the infinite dihedral group.

For each positive integer \(m\), consider all plane triangulations with exactly \(m\) vertices. Given such a triangulation \(H\), write \(p(H)\) for the largest size of a collection of pairwise vertex-disjoint three-vertex paths in \(H\), and define
\[
a_m=\frac{1}{m}\min\{p(H):H\text{ is a plane triangulation with }m\text{ vertices}\}.
\]
What is the exact value of the limit inferior of \(a_m\) as \(m\) tends to infinity?

For a finite simple graph \(H\), define its girth to be the number of edges in a shortest cycle, taking this value to be infinity when \(H\) has no cycles.

Let \(M(r)\) be the maximum chromatic number among all finite simple graphs \(H\) whose complement has girth greater than five and whose cliques each contain at most \(r\) vertices. What is the exact value of \(M(6)\)?

For a set \(A\) of positive integers, call a hypergraph an \(A\)-hypergraph when every edge has size in \(A\). For a hypergraph \(G\), write \(d_k(G)\) for the least number of edges containing any fixed set of \(k\) vertices, where the minimum is taken over all such vertex sets.

Write \(T_\ell^{(q)}\) for the \(q\)-uniform tight cycle on \(\ell\) vertices: it has at least three edges, and its vertices can be arranged around a circle so that each block of \(q\) consecutive vertices is an edge. A hypergraph \(G\) is a Berge copy of a hypergraph \(J\) if there are an injective vertex map \(\phi\) from \(J\) to \(G\) and a bijective edge map \(\psi\) from \(J\) to \(G\), with the property that \(\phi(x)\) lies in \(\psi(a)\) whenever \(x\) is a vertex of the edge \(a\).

Determine the smallest positive integer \(N\) with the following property: for every integer \(m\) at least \(N\), every hypergraph on \(m\) vertices whose edges have sizes one, two, three, or four, and for which \(d_3(G)\) is at least one, contains a Berge copy of \(T_\ell^{(3)}\) for each integer \(\ell\) from four through \(m\), inclusive.
Determine the exact number of distinct partial-order relations on a fixed set of nineteen labeled elements.

Define integers \(a_t\) by the formal generating function
\[
\sum_{t\ge 0} a_t z^t
=
\sum_{k\ge 0} z^{\,2k^2+2k}
\prod_{i=1}^{k+1}\frac{1-z^{2i-1}}{1-z^{6i-3}}.
\]
Find the sum of all nonnegative indices \(t\) for which the coefficient \(a_t\) vanishes.

Suppose infinitely many triangles have all three vertices on a fixed circle \(\Gamma\), with each of their side lines tangent to a fixed conic \(Q\), where \(Q\) is either an ellipse or a hyperbola. Prove that the sum of the squares of the three side lengths is the same for every triangle in this Poncelet family if and only if \(\Gamma\) and \(Q\) have a common center.

Choose parameters \(a\) and \(h\) satisfying \(1<a<2\) and \(\tfrac12<h\leq1\), and let \(\lambda>0\). On the real line, consider the mild solution, with the stochastic term interpreted in the Skorohod sense, of
\[
\partial_\tau v(\tau,z)+(-\Delta)^{a/2}v(\tau,z)
=\lambda\,\eta(\tau)\,\delta_0(z)\,v(\tau,z),
\qquad v(0,z)=f(z),
\]
where \(f\) is bounded and measurable, \(-(-\Delta)^{a/2}\) denotes the fractional Laplacian, and \(\delta_0\) is the Dirac delta at the origin. The Gaussian noise \(\eta\) has covariance
\[
\mathbb E[\eta(r)\eta(q)]=|r-q|^{-2(1-h)}.
\]
Whenever \(2h>1+a^{-1}\), this equation has a unique global solution in \(L^2\).

Let \(F\) be a finite field of odd prime-power order \(r>3\), and put \(h=(r-1)/2\). Consider the full affine group
\[
G=\{\,x\mapsto ax+b:\ a\in F^\times,\ b\in F\,\}.
\]
If \(r\) has remainder \(1\) upon division by \(4\), then \(G\) is the full automorphism group of chiral polyhedra of types \(\{2h,h\}\) and \(\{h,2h\}\). If that remainder is \(3\), then \(G\) is the full automorphism group of a chiral polyhedron of type \(\{2h,2h\}\).

In Euclidean space of dimension \(d\), write \(A_{\mathrm{trop}}^{d-1}\) for the tropical spherical measure induced by the tropical metric, and \(B_{\mathrm{trop}}^{d-1}\) for the tropical Minkowski surface measure.
