Call a set \(d\)-admissible if it is compact, has dimension \(d\), and has a rectifiable boundary of dimension \(d-1\) and finite perimeter. Show that
\[
B_{\mathrm{trop}}^{d-1}(\partial K)
=
A_{\mathrm{trop}}^{d-1}(\partial K)
\]
whenever \(K\) is a full-dimensional convex polytope in \(\mathbb{R}^{d}\), and also whenever \(d=2\) and \(K\) is a \(2\)-admissible subset of the plane.

Consider a velocity field \(v(y,s)\) satisfying the incompressible Navier–Stokes system in \(n\) spatial dimensions on a periodic domain, driven by a time-independent force \(g(y)\). Suppose the smooth initial velocity and the forcing share a spatial symmetry consisting of translation of a coordinate by one-half of its period, reflection through a point, or both. Assume also that, about every nonnegative time, the Taylor expansion of the velocity in time exists and converges within a strictly positive radius.

In two spatial dimensions, the velocity retains the shared spatial symmetry at every positive time. In three spatial dimensions, however, there are configurations meeting all these hypotheses for which the velocity spontaneously breaks that symmetry at a finite, strictly positive time.

Fix an integer \(d>3\), and write \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\) for the Frobenius norm on complex \(d\times d\) matrices. Given such a matrix \(T\), let
\[
H=(T^*T)^{1/2},\qquad T=VH
\]
be its polar decomposition. For a real parameter \(t\in(0,1)\), set
\[
B_t=H^tVH^{\,1-t},
\]
the \(t\)-Aluthge transform of \(T\).

Show that, for every choice of \(T\) and \(t\) as above,
\[
\bigl\|B_tB_t^*-B_t^*B_t\bigr\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
\le
\bigl\|TT^*-T^*T\bigr\|_{\mathrm{HS}}.
\]

Suppose that \(\mathfrak{a}\) is a simple Lie algebra of simply-laced type, and choose a nilpotent element \(e\) of \(\mathfrak{a}\). At every nonrational complex level \(t\), quantum Hamiltonian reduction with respect to \(e\) yields an equivalence of abelian categories
\[
\mathrm{KL}\!\left(V^{t}(\mathfrak{a})\right)
\;\simeq\;
\mathrm{KL}\!\left(W^{t}(\mathfrak{a},e)\right),
\]
where \(\mathrm{KL}\) denotes the Kazhdan–Lusztig category of the indicated affine vertex algebra or \(W\)-algebra. This reduction functor admits the structure of a braided tensor equivalence precisely when \(e\) is principal, or equivalently, regular nilpotent.

Suppose \(B\) is a self-injective Nakayama algebra over a field \(F\). Show that the Nakayama automorphism of \(B\) is semisimple if and only if the Hochschild cohomology ring of \(B\) is a Batalin–Vilkovisky algebra.

Let \(k\) and \(m\) be positive integers with \(m>k\). Show that there is a nonempty \(k\)-pseudoconcave set \(E\subseteq\mathbb{C}^{m}\) containing no complex submanifold of complex dimension \(k\), while locally \(E\) can be represented as the graph of a continuous function defined on a closed subset of \(\mathbb{C}^{k}\times\mathbb{R}\).

Suppose \(K\) is a framed link with \(r\) components in the three-sphere. Assume that surgery with the prescribed framings yields a connected sum of \(r\) three-manifolds, each with the same homology as the product of a circle and a two-sphere. Then \(K\) is equivalent, under handleslides, to a split link with \(r\) components.

Write \(e_1,e_2,e_3\) for the standard basis of Euclidean three-space, and consider the tetrahedron with corners
\[
p_0=\mathbf 0,\qquad p_1=e_3,\qquad p_2=e_2+e_3,\qquad p_3=e_1+e_2+e_3.
\]
For each index \(j=0,1,2,3\), introduce the contraction
\[
T_j(u)=\tfrac12u+\tfrac12p_j.
\]
The Sierpiński tetrahedron \(K\) is the unique nonempty compact set whose images under these four contractions have union \(K\).

Given a height \(t\) between zero and one, inclusive, define its horizontal section by
\[
H_t=\{u\in K:\langle u,e_3\rangle=t\}.
\]
For irrational \(t\), the section \(H_t\) is totally disconnected, and its Čech homology groups in every positive degree vanish. For rational \(t\), the section \(H_t\) has finitely many connected components and an infinite first Čech homology group.

Call a scheme \(Y\) of finite type over the integers a *polynomial count variety* if there are a nonzero integer \(m\) and a polynomial \(P(u)\) such that, for every finite field \(k\) whose characteristic does not divide \(m\), the number of \(k\)-rational points of \(Y\) is \(P(|k|)\).

Suppose \(Y\) has this property, its base change to the complex numbers is smooth, and \(P(u)=u^d\) for an integer \(d\geq 1\). Then this complex scheme is isomorphic to
\[
\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbb{C}[z_1,\ldots,z_d]\bigr).
\]

Let \(Y\) be a closed, shift-invariant collection of one-sided sequences over a finite alphabet \(B\). Assume that the probability measures supported on periodic orbits are dense among all shift-invariant probability measures on \(Y\).

Prove that Typical Periodic Optimization holds in the Lipschitz category: the space of real-valued Lipschitz observables on \(Y\) has an open dense subset \(\mathcal U\) such that every \(g\in\mathcal U\) admits exactly one shift-invariant probability measure maximizing its integral, and that measure is supported on a single periodic orbit.

Suppose a Banach space \(E\) admits an unconditional basis, and assume that any two normalized unconditional bases of \(E\) become equivalent after permuting the vectors of one of them. Prove that \(E\) is isomorphic to the direct sum of two copies of itself.

Write \(\Delta=\{\xi\in\mathbb C:|\xi|<1\}\), and regard the Hardy space \(\mathcal H=H^2(\Delta\times\Delta)\) as a module over \(\mathbb C[u,v]\). For a nonconstant homogeneous polynomial \(q(u,v)\), let
\[
\mathcal M_q=\overline{\{qf:f\in\mathbb C[u,v]\}}^{\,\mathcal H}.
\]
Prove that the quotient module \(\mathcal H/\mathcal M_q\) is subnormal precisely when no irreducible factor of \(q\) occurs more than once.

Consider a finite ring of local quantum systems. An automorphism of their tensor-product algebra is called an approximate one-dimensional quantum cellular automaton (QCA) when it respects locality up to a small error. Strict one-dimensional QCAs are classified by one topological index, but the approximate setting on a finite ring has a richer classification. In particular, some approximate QCAs admit no rounding to a strict QCA; the obstruction to such a rounding gives a secondary topological index valued in the cyclic group of order two.

Call a map \(\varphi:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\) a gauge if it is right-continuous, nondecreasing, and tends to zero as its argument decreases to zero. Say that a function \(u\) eventually dominates a function \(v\) when \(v(t)\leq u(t)\) for every sufficiently small positive \(t\).

Let \(\mathcal I\) be a nonempty countable collection of reals that is closed under Turing joins and downward closed under Turing reducibility. Show that, for any gauge \(\varphi\), the collection of \(\mathcal I\)-Mathias generics has positive Hausdorff measure with gauge \(\varphi\) precisely when no gauge belonging to \(\mathcal I\) eventually dominates \(\varphi\).

Consider a bounded sequence of complex numbers \((a_k)_{k\ge 1}\) and the non-autonomous iteration obtained by applying, at step \(k\), the cubic map
\[
P_k(w)=w\bigl(w^2+a_k\bigr).
\]
If the Julia set of this sequence of maps is totally disconnected, then the resulting non-autonomous dynamical system is hyperbolic.

Suppose \(V\) is a holomorphic vector bundle on a compact Kähler manifold \(M\), and let \(\beta\) be a nef and big class on \(M\). Assume that, with respect to \(\beta\), the bundle \(V\) is slope polystable and equality holds in the Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality. Show that \(V\) is projectively flat everywhere on \(M\).

Let \(\mathcal{U}=\{w\in\mathbb{C}:|w|<1\}\), and denote its Bergman space by \(\mathcal{B}^{2}(\mathcal{U})\). Suppose \(h\) is a bounded, real-valued radial symbol, with associated Toeplitz operator \(S_h\) and Berezin transform \(\mathfrak{B}h\).

Prove that if the lower limit of \((\mathfrak{B}h)(w)\) as \(|w|\) approaches one from below is nonnegative, then every point in the essential spectrum of \(S_h\) is a nonnegative real number.

On the square integer lattice, let \(P\) be a real-valued potential with period \(p_1\) in the first coordinate and period \(p_2\) in the second. Write \(L\) for the discrete Laplacian and \(T_P\) for the operator obtained by adding multiplication by \(P\) to \(L\).

For each complex energy \(E\), define \(\mathcal S_E(P)\) to be the set of vectors \(\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in\mathbb C^2\) for which there is a nonzero lattice function \(\psi\) satisfying
\[
(L\psi)(m)+(P(m)-E)\psi(m)=0
\]
at every lattice point \(m\), together with the conditions
\[
\exp(2\pi i\theta_r)\,\psi(m)=\psi(m+p_r\varepsilon_r),
\qquad r\in\{1,2\},
\]
where \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\) are the standard coordinate vectors. Two potentials are called Fermi isospectral at energy \(E\) when their sets \(\mathcal S_E\) coincide.

Prove that if \(\mathcal S_0(P)=\mathcal S_0(0)\), then \(P\) vanishes at every lattice point.

Suppose \(F\) is a field of positive characteristic \(\ell\), and \(A\) is a finite abelian \(\ell\)-group whose minimal number of generators is even. Let \(V\) be an \(FA\)-module expressible as a direct sum of syzygies and cosyzygies of the trivial \(FA\)-module \(F\).

For each nonnegative integer \(j\), let \(d_j\) denote the \(F\)-dimension of what remains of the \(j\)-fold tensor power of \(V\) after its projective direct summands are removed. Show that \((d_j)\) satisfies a linear recurrence for all sufficiently large indices. Equivalently, prove that the formal power series
\[
D(z)=d_0+d_1z+d_2z^2+\cdots
\]
is rational.

Suppose \(H\) is a \(2\)-connected graph with \(N\) vertices, where \(N\) is an integer no smaller than four. Assume every vertex has degree at least the square root of \(N\). Show that for each integer \(t\) from four through \(N\), the graph \(H\) contains a \(2\)-connected subgraph with exactly \(t\) vertices.

Let \(S\) be an arbitrary closed surface. Prove that the space of continuously differentiable diffeomorphisms of \(S\), endowed with the \(C^1\) topology, contains an open dense subset \(\mathcal U\) whose continuum-wise expansive elements are all Anosov diffeomorphisms.

For each integer \(d\) at least \(3{,}000{,}000{,}000\), there is a graph \(H\) whose maximum degree and correspondence chromatic number are both \(d\), and in which every clique has fewer than \(d\) vertices.

Let a particle have position \(x\) and momentum \(r\) in \(\mathbb{R}^{n}\), and let its dynamics be governed by a non-Markovian generalized relativistic Langevin equation. Suppose its memory kernel is a finite linear combination of exponential functions. The external potential \(V\) is smooth, takes values in \([1,\infty)\), and, for some positive constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3\) and an exponent \(\kappa\geq 1\), satisfies, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\),
\[
c_1\|x\|^{1+\kappa}\leq x\cdot\nabla V(x)+c_2,
\]
together with the growth bounds
\[
c_3^{-1}\|x\|^{1+\kappa}\leq V(x)+c_3,
\qquad
V(x)\leq c_3+c_3\|x\|^{1+\kappa}.
\]
Under these assumptions, the equivalent Markovian formulation obtained by adjoining auxiliary variables is well-posed and geometrically ergodic: it has a unique Gibbs distribution, to which it converges exponentially fast in total variation distance.

Given a 3-uniform hypergraph \(H\), let \(R_H(t)\) denote the least integer \(M\) for which every 3-uniform hypergraph on \(M\) vertices containing no copy of \(H\) has an independent set with \(t\) vertices. Then one of the following holds:

- There is a polynomial \(q\) such that \(R_H(t)\le q(t)\) for every \(t\).
- There is a positive constant \(\varepsilon\) such that \(R_H(t)\ge \exp\!\bigl((\log 2)t^\varepsilon\bigr)\) for all sufficiently large \(t\).

For a graph \(H\) with vertex set \(W\), assign to each vertex an integer label between zero and three, inclusive. The weight of a labeling is the sum of all its labels.

Call such a labeling **double Roman dominating** when both of the following requirements hold:
- Every vertex labeled one has a neighbor labeled at least two.
- Every vertex labeled zero has either a neighbor labeled three or at least two neighbors labeled two.

Write \(R(H)\) for the smallest weight of a double Roman dominating labeling of \(H\).

A labeling is **double Italian dominating** if, at each vertex labeled zero or one, the total of its own label and the labels of all its neighbors is at least three. Write \(I(H)\) for the smallest weight of a labeling satisfying this requirement.

Prove that every tree \(S\) satisfies
\[
I(S)=R(S).
\]
Every strongly irreducible subshift over the lattice \(\mathbb{Z}^{n}\), with \(n\) any positive integer, has a residually finite automorphism group.

Let \(E\) be the finite state space of a discrete-time imprecise Markov chain. Assume that its family of transition matrices is convex and compact, with separately specified rows. Fix a target set \(B\subseteq E\).

For a starting state \(y\), write \(H_-(y)\) and \(H_+(y)\) for the lower and upper expected times to hit \(B\), respectively, and write \(q_-(y)\) and \(q_+(y)\) for the corresponding lower and upper probabilities of ever hitting \(B\).

Show that, for every \(y\in E\),
\[
q_+(y)=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H_-(y)<+\infty.
\]

Write \(\mathsf K\) for weak Kőnig’s lemma. In the Weihrauch ordering, the Hahn–Banach theorem restricted to the fixed Banach space of absolutely summable sequences is strictly weaker than \(\mathsf K\). By contrast, when the Banach space is allowed to vary, the Hahn–Banach theorem is Weihrauch equivalent to \(\mathsf K\).

Let \(H\) be an arbitrary simply connected simple algebraic group. Consider the Schubert scheme constructed by Finkelberg–Mirković inside its affine Grassmannian, corresponding to the quasi-minuscule coweight. Show that this scheme is reduced.

Suppose a surface \(\Sigma\) in the three-dimensional future light cone is an entire graph over a horosphere. Prove that if its Gaussian curvature is bounded from below and its mean curvature is constant, then \(\Sigma\) is itself a horosphere in that light cone.

Consider a probability space \((X,\mathscr A,\mu)\) equipped with a measure-preserving transformation \(T\). Let \(g\) be a measurable family of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the circle, viewed as the real line modulo integer translations, and let this family define a discrete-time random dynamical system.

For each \(\xi\in X\), choose the normalized lift \(G_\xi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) of \(g_\xi\), characterized by
\[
0\leq G_\xi(0)<1.
\]
Assume that the displacement of these lifts is integrable:
\[
\mathbb E_\mu\!\left[\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|G_\xi(t)-t|\right]<\infty.
\]
Write
\[
G_\xi^{[k]}=G_{T^{k-1}\xi}\circ\cdots\circ G_\xi
\]
for the lifted random iterates.

Suppose there is a point \(p\) on the circle that is fixed by \(g_\xi\) for every \(\xi\in X\). Show that the mean random rotation number
\[
r(G):=\mathbb E_\mu\!\left[\lim_{k\to\infty}k^{-1}G_\xi^{[k]}(0)\right]
\]
belongs to \(\mathbb Z\).

Consider the pentagram transformation \(T\) on planar polygons, obtained by intersecting their diagonals. Prove that if applying \(T\) twice to a pentagon \(Q\) produces a translated and uniformly scaled copy of \(Q\), then \(Q\) is the image of a regular pentagon under an affine transformation.

Define **Rank-\(k\) Constrained Nonnegative Gram Feasibility** as the following decision problem. The input consists of an integer \(m\), prescribed values for some entries of a symmetric matrix \(A\) of order \(m\), and affine constraints involving its entries. Is there a collection of vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\), each with \(k\) nonnegative real coordinates, such that assigning
\[
A_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle \qquad (1\le i,j\le m)
\]
obeys every prescribed value and every affine constraint?

This problem admits a polynomial-time algorithm when \(k\) is two, whereas for each fixed integer \(k\) of at least three it is complete for \(\exists\mathbb{R}\).

Suppose \(S\) is a connected, locally compact metric space, and \((Y_j)_{j\geq 0}\) is a Markov chain on \(S\). Its transition operator \(P\) is Feller on \(C_b(S)\); thus, writing \(\mathbb E_s\) for expectation when the chain starts at \(s\),
\[
(Pf)(s)=\mathbb E_s[f(Y_1)].
\]
Assume that the chain has exactly one stationary probability measure, denoted by \(\pi\).

Call the chain an e-chain when, for each compactly supported continuous function \(f\), the iterates \(P^m f\), with \(m\) ranging over the natural numbers, form an equicontinuous family on every compact subset of \(S\).

Prove that the e-chain property implies the following strong law of large numbers: for every starting point \(s\in S\) and every \(f\in C_c(S)\),
\[
\mathbb P_s\!\left(
\lim_{N\to\infty}
\left[\frac{f(Y_1)+\cdots+f(Y_N)}{N}
-\int_S f(u)\,\pi(du)\right]=0
\right)=1.
\]

Fix a dimension \(d\in\{1,\ldots,9\}\) and exponents \(a,b\) satisfying \(1\le a<b\le\infty\). For \(r>0\), write
\[
D_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:|y|<r\}.
\]
A classical solution \(v\) of
\[
\Delta v+g(v)=0\qquad\text{in }D_1
\]
is said to be stable when
\[
\int_{D_1}g'(v)\varphi^2\,dy
\le
\int_{D_1}|\nabla\varphi|^2\,dy
\]
for every \(\varphi\in C_0^1(\overline{D_1})\) that vanishes on \(\partial D_1\).

Show that a positive constant \(K\), determined solely by \(d,a,b\), exists such that every smooth nonlinearity \(g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) and every stable solution \(v\in C^\infty(\overline{D_1})\) of this equation satisfy
\[
K\,\|v\|_{L^a(D_1)}
\ge
\|v\|_{L^b(D_{1/2})}.
\]

Suppose \((Y,\mathcal A,\nu)\) is a non-atomic measure space with \(\nu(Y)<\infty\), and choose exponents \(r,s\) satisfying \(1\le r<s<\infty\). Let \(a:Y\to\mathbb C\) be measurable and let \(\psi:Y\to Y\) be measurable and non-singular. Define the associated weighted composition map by
\[
(Tg)(y)=a(y)\,g(\psi(y)).
\]
There exist nonzero nuclear operators of this form mapping \(L^s(\nu)\) into \(L^r(\nu)\).

Suppose \(H:\mathbb{C}^{3}\to\mathbb{C}\) is holomorphic everywhere, and its slices \(w\mapsto H(w,s,t)\), as \((s,t)\) ranges over \(\mathbb{C}^{2}\), form a normal family on the whole complex plane. Show that there are entire maps \(\psi:\mathbb{C}^{2}\to\mathbb{C}\) and \(K:\mathbb{C}^{2}\to\mathbb{C}\) for which
\[
K\bigl(w,\psi(s,t)\bigr)=H(w,s,t)
\qquad\text{for every }(w,s,t)\in\mathbb{C}^{3}.
\]

A commutative association scheme admits a multivariate P-polynomial structure (respectively, Q-polynomial structure) relative to a monomial order of elimination type precisely when it can be expressed as a direct product of univariate P-polynomial schemes (respectively, Q-polynomial schemes).

Take a finite field \(K\) of prime-power order \(r\), a positive integer \(m\), and an integer \(t\) with \(m\ge t\ge 2\). Define a graph \(H\) on the length-\(m\) vectors over \(K\) by joining two distinct vectors when they differ in fewer than \(t\) coordinates. Thus, in the complement \(H^{c}\), two vectors are joined precisely when they differ in at least \(t\) coordinates.

Prove that \(H^{c}\) is edge-transitive if and only if it is distance-transitive.

Suppose \(Q\) consists of \(m\) points in the plane, all in convex position. Form a graph \(\mathcal{G}_Q\) whose vertices represent the non-crossing spanning trees with vertex set \(Q\). Two vertices are adjacent precisely when one represented tree is obtained from the other by deleting one edge and inserting another. Given any two such trees, their shortest-path distance in \(\mathcal{G}_Q\) can be computed in polynomial time.

Suppose a Banach space \(E\) has a closed linear subspace \(F\) such that both \(F\) and the quotient \(E/F\) are isomorphic to the same Hilbert space \(K\). Such an \(E\) is called a twisted Hilbert space. Show that \(E\) is isomorphic to its continuous dual, denoted by \(E'\).

Suppose \(X\) is a closed smooth manifold. Choose any Riemannian metric on \(X\) and any Morse function \(f\colon X\to\mathbb{R}\). Show that the classifying space of the Morse flow category determined by these choices has the same homotopy type as \(X\).

Let \(d\) be any integer greater than one. If a CAT(0) space \(Y\) is quasi-isometric to \(d\)-dimensional Euclidean space and is both proper and geodesically complete, then \(Y\) is homeomorphic to \(d\)-dimensional Euclidean space.

Every finite collection of first-order sentences that hold in the Farey graph is simultaneously satisfied by some finite planar graph. In particular, the first-order theory of the Farey graph is pseudofinite, with finite planar graphs witnessing this property.

For a countable group \(\Gamma\), call a sequence of matrix-valued maps strongly convergent when the norm of every polynomial in the images of group elements tends to the norm of the corresponding polynomial in the left regular representation. The group is called **MF** (matricial field) if it has such a sequence consisting of approximate homomorphisms. It is called **PMF** (purely MF) if the maps can all be taken to be genuine homomorphisms, and **PFF** (purely finite field) if, in addition, each of these homomorphisms has finite image.

Show that every closed hyperbolic three-manifold has a PMF fundamental group, whereas some closed hyperbolic three-manifolds have fundamental groups that are not PFF.

Suppose \((N,h,V)\) is a complete expanding gradient Ricci soliton whose metric is asymptotically conical. Prove that if its tangent cone at infinity carries a Kähler cone structure, then \((N,h,V)\) is a Kähler–Ricci soliton.

For a graph \(H\), suppose a set \(A(x)\) of exactly \(r\) colors is prescribed at every vertex \(x\). A packing for these lists consists of \(r\) proper colorings \(c_1,\dots,c_r\) of \(H\), each using only prescribed colors, such that at each vertex the colors used by the \(r\) colorings are all distinct and exhaust its prescribed set.

Write \(p(H)\) for the least integer \(r\) for which every choice of lists of size \(r\) admits such a packing. For an integer \(b\), let
\[
M(b)=\max\bigl\{p(H):\operatorname{tw}(H)\le b\bigr\}.
\]
Show that, whenever \(b\) is an integer at least two,
\[
M(b)+1\le 2b.
\]

Fix an integer \(d>1\), and write \(\mathcal A=\mathbb C^{d\times d}\). For a linear subspace \(V\subseteq\mathcal A\), define its structured singular value at \(T\in\mathcal A\) by
\[
s_V(T)=\left(\inf_{\substack{Y\in V\\1\in\sigma(TY)}}\|Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right)^{-1},
\]
where \(\sigma(TY)\) is the spectrum of \(TY\) and \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) is the operator norm. Set \(s_V(T)=0\) when no \(Y\in V\) makes \(1\) an eigenvalue of \(TY\).

Prove that any linear subspace \(W\subseteq\mathcal A\) satisfying
\[
s_W(T)=\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\qquad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal A
\]
must be the entire space \(\mathcal A\).

Prove that every complete Riemannian surface \(M\) with no boundary admits a triangulation \(\mathcal T\) with the following property: if the graph consisting of the vertices and edges of \(\mathcal T\) is given the path metric in which each edge has unit length, then its natural inclusion into \(M\), endowed with its Riemannian distance, is a quasi-isometry.

Consider a rational arrival process represented by real matrices \(A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) and a real row vector \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times d}\). Let \(u\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\) have every entry equal to one. For each positive integer \(m\), its joint density is
\[
p_m(s_1,\ldots,s_m)
=\alpha\left[\prod_{j=1}^{m}\bigl(\exp(s_jA)B\bigr)\right]u,
\qquad (s_1,\ldots,s_m)\in[0,\infty)^m,
\]
where the factors are ordered by increasing \(j\) from left to right.

Suppose that \(Bu=-Au\), that \(A\) has a unique dominant eigenvalue which is real, and that every density \(p_m\) is strictly positive throughout its stated domain. Then this process has an equivalent finite-dimensional Markovian arrival process representation.

Consider a cone \(Q\) in \(d\)-dimensional Euclidean space, generated over a closed, strictly convex manifold that is three times continuously differentiable and has a nondegenerate second fundamental form. Viewed as a discrete-time Hamiltonian system, the billiard dynamics within \(Q\) is completely integrable precisely when \(Q\) is a quadric or is made up of pieces of quadrics.

Suppose \((N,h)\) is a compact static three-dimensional manifold with nonempty boundary and admits two linearly independent static potentials. Show that there is a static potential \(v\) which vanishes at some point in the interior of \(N\) but is nowhere zero on \(\partial N\).

Let \(H_N\) be an Erdős–Rényi graph on \(N\) vertices, with each edge present independently with probability \(\lambda/N\), where the mean degree satisfies \(\lambda>1\). Place the Ising model on \(H_N\) at its critical temperature. For spins \(s=(s_1,\ldots,s_N)\in\{-1,+1\}^{N}\), write the total magnetization as
\[
S_N=s_1+\cdots+s_N.
\]
As \(N\) tends to infinity, the quenched distribution of \(S_N/N^{3/4}\) converges in distribution, with respect to the \(1\)-Wasserstein distance induced by the Kolmogorov–Smirnov metric, to a deterministic probability measure whose density is
\[
f(x)=K^{-1}e^{-a x^{4}},
\]
where \(a>0\) and \(K\) is the normalizing constant.

Grow a random recursive tree from a single root labelled \(0\). At stage \(m=1,2,\ldots\), add vertex \(m\), choose its parent uniformly among the \(m\) vertices already present, and independently keep the new edge with probability \(q\), where \(0<q\leq 1\). This growth construction couples the Bernoulli bond-percolation configurations over all stages.

Write \(H(q)\) for the probability that, at every stage, the component containing the root has at least as many vertices as any other component. There is a threshold \(q_\star\), strictly between zero and one, for which
\[
H(q)=
\begin{cases}
0, & 0<q<q_\star,\\
\text{a strictly positive value}, & q_\star<q\leq 1.
\end{cases}
\]
Any ribbon knot admits a presentation as a symmetric union.

Let \(K\) be a link with two or more components in the three-sphere, and write \(\Gamma\) for the fundamental group of its complement. Prove that \(K\) is fibered if and only if the derived subgroup of \(\Gamma\) is finitely generated.

Suppose \(D\) is a bounded, convex, open subset of \(\mathbb{R}^{d}\), and \(W\) is a smooth convex potential on \(D\). Let \(\phi\) be the positive eigenfunction corresponding to the lowest eigenvalue of the operator
\[
f\longmapsto Wf-\Delta f
\]
with Dirichlet boundary conditions, scaled so that \(\sup_{y\in D}|\phi(y)|=1\).

Prove that \(\phi\) is one-half-logconcave; equivalently, show that
\[
y\longmapsto \left(\log\frac{1}{\phi(y)}\right)^{1/2}
\]
is convex throughout \(D\).

Suppose \(m\) is an integer greater than two and \(K\) is a hyperbolic link in the three-sphere with \(m\) components. Let \(E\) be the complement of the interior of a regular neighborhood of \(K\).

If an incompressible planar surface \(\Sigma\) in \(E\) has precisely one boundary circle on each torus of \(\partial E\), then some boundary circle of \(\Sigma\) has either meridional or integral slope. Equivalently, writing that slope as \(r/s\) in the standard meridian–longitude coordinates, its denominator \(s\) is zero or one.

Prove that, for each integer \(n\) greater than two, one can find a countable group \(\Gamma\), a finite symmetric generating set \(A\subseteq\Gamma\), a probability measure \(p\) whose support generates \(\Gamma\) as a semigroup, and a Borel probability measure \(\eta\) on the Chabauty space \(\operatorname{Sub}(\Gamma)\) with the following properties:

- Writing \(c_x(L)=xLx^{-1}\) for conjugation by \(x\in\Gamma\), the measure \(\eta\) is \(p\)-stationary:
  \[
  \sum_{x\in\Gamma}p(x)\,(c_x)_*\eta=\eta.
  \]
- For \(\eta\)-almost every subgroup \(L\leq\Gamma\), the Schreier graph whose vertices are the right cosets of \(L\), and which has an edge from \(Lx\) to \(Lxa\) for every \(x\in\Gamma\) and \(a\in A\), has precisely \(n\) ends.

Suppose \(S\) is a projective surface that is hyperbolic in the sense of Kobayashi. The existence on \(S\) of a Hermitian metric whose holomorphic sectional curvature is negative in every holomorphic tangent direction forces the Kähler–Einstein metric on \(S\) to have this same curvature property.

Construct a rooted tree \(G\) whose vertices are integer pairs \((r,s)\) with \(r\ge s\ge0\), taking the pair of zeros as the root \(o\). Join each \((r,0)\) to \((r+1,0)\), forming an infinite spine. For every positive integer \(r\), attach to \((r,0)\) the path through \((r,1),\ldots,(r,r)\). There are no other edges.

Fix a parameter \(a\in(0,1)\), and let \((Y_m)_{m\ge0}\) be a nearest-neighbor random walk on \(G\). At a non-root vertex with \(k\) children, the walk moves to its parent with probability \(a/(a+k)\) and to each child with probability \(1/(a+k)\). From the root it moves to its sole neighbor.

Writing \(d(o,v)\) for graph distance from the root, show that
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{d(o,Y_m)}{\ln m}
=-\frac{1}{\ln a}
\qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]

Suppose \(H\) is a connected graph with \(m\) vertices and diameter exactly two. Write \(\rho(x,y)\) for the distance between vertices \(x\) and \(y\), and define
\[
\tau(x)=\sum_{y\in V(H)}\rho(x,y),
\qquad
\mathcal W(H)=\frac12\sum_{x,y\in V(H)}\rho(x,y).
\]
Let \(R=(\rho(x,y))_{x,y\in V(H)}\), and form the distance Laplacian
\[
\mathcal L=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\tau(x):x\in V(H)\bigr)-R.
\]
List its eigenvalues in nonincreasing order as \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m\). Show that, for every integer \(k\) between \(1\) and \(m\),
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{k}\mu_j-\mathcal W(H)
\le \frac{k(k+1)(k+2)}{6}.
\]

Recall that a linearly ordered structure is called weakly o-minimal when each definable subset of its underlying set can be expressed as a finite union of convex subsets.

Suppose \(\mathcal{N}\) is a weakly o-minimal expansion of an ordered field with underlying set \(K\). Prove that, given an open definable subset \(V\) of \(K\) and a definable map \(g:V\to K\), one can find an open interval \(J\) contained in \(V\) such that \(g\) is differentiable at every point of \(J\).

For a graph \(H\), write \(\rho(H)\) for the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. Fix \(q\in(1,2]\), and define
\[
D_q(H):=\max_{\emptyset\neq T\subseteq V(H)}
|T|^{-q}\,\bigl|E(H[T])\bigr|,
\]
where \(H[T]\) is the subgraph induced by \(T\).

Show that there is a positive constant \(K_q\), depending only on \(q\), such that every graph \(H\) on \(m\) vertices containing at least one edge obeys
\[
\rho(H)\le \bigl(K_q+o(1)\bigr)\,D_q(H)\,
\max\!\left\{\sqrt m,\;m^{q-1}\right\}
\qquad\text{as }m\to\infty.
\]

For a finite set \(S\), say that an operation \(h:S^m\to S\) admits a polynomial representation with degree bound \(D\) over a commutative ring \(A\) if there are a one-to-one map \(\iota:S\to A\) and a polynomial \(P\in A[t_1,\ldots,t_m]\) whose total degree does not exceed \(D\), satisfying
\[
P\bigl(\iota(a_1),\ldots,\iota(a_m)\bigr)
=\iota\bigl(h(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\bigr)
\]
for every choice of \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) in \(S\).

There is a positive integer \(D\), independent of both the finite set \(S\) and the binary operation \(h:S\times S\to S\), such that every such operation admits a polynomial representation with degree bound \(D\) over some commutative ring \(A\).

Let \(F\) be a number field, and let \(Y\) be a homogeneous space over \(F\) under the special linear group of degree \(m\). Suppose that its geometric stabilizers are finite and nilpotent.

Assume that the unramified Brauer classes on \(Y\) which become trivial after extension to an algebraic closure of \(F\) are exactly the classes in the image of the natural map from the Brauer group of \(F\) to that of \(Y\). Assume also that \(Y(F_w)\) is nonempty for every place \(w\) of \(F\).

Show that \(Y\) admits an \(F\)-rational point.

Given a graph \(H\), write \(E_H(N)\) for the largest possible edge count of an \(H\)-free graph on \(N\) vertices. Define \(M_H(N,s)\) as the least number of subgraphs isomorphic to \(H\) among all graphs on \(N\) vertices having \(s+E_H(N)\) edges. Also, let \(A_H(N)\) be the least number of such copies obtainable by inserting a single new edge into an \(N\)-vertex \(H\)-free graph with \(E_H(N)\) edges.

Whenever \(H\) has a cycle, there is a threshold \(N_0\) such that
\[
A_H(N)=M_H(N,1)
\qquad\text{for every integer }N\ge N_0.
\]

Consider a tropical abelian variety \(T\): a real torus \(\mathbb{R}^{m}/\mathbb{Z}^{m}\) endowed with a positive-definite quadratic form on its covering vector space. Suppose \(Y\subseteq T\) is a tropical subvariety of pure dimension \(r\), represented by a weighted, embedded rational polyhedral complex with integral slopes and satisfying the balancing condition. Then the topological Euler characteristic of \(Y\) is nonnegative when \(r\) is even and nonpositive when \(r\) is odd.

Let \(S\) be an algebraic torus over the rational numbers and let \(\ell\) be any prime. Write \(K_\ell\) for the maximal compact subgroup of \(S(\mathbb{Q}_\ell)\). Show that each \(x\in S(\mathbb{Q}_\ell)\) admits a factorization \(x=ks\), where \(k\in K_\ell\) and \(s\in S(\mathbb{Q})\).

Consider structures with two sorts: a point set \(P\) and a linearly ordered distance set \(\Lambda_P\) whose minimum is denoted by \(\bot_P\). The distance function \(\rho_P:P^2\to\Lambda_P\) is symmetric, takes the value \(\bot_P\) exactly on the diagonal, and satisfies the following condition: for any three points, the distance between the first and third is no greater than the larger of the other two pairwise distances.

A dc-embedding of such a structure \(P\) into another such structure \(Q\) is a pair \((e,\eta)\), where \(e\) injects the point set of \(P\) into that of \(Q\), and \(\eta\) is an order-preserving injection of their distance sets that sends the least element to the least element. These maps must satisfy
\[
\eta\bigl(\rho_P(u,v)\bigr)=\rho_Q\bigl(e(u),e(v)\bigr)
\qquad(u,v\in P).
\]

Let \(\mathcal M\) be the Fraïssé limit of the class of all finite structures of this kind, using dc-embeddings. Prove that \(G=\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal M)\) has ample generics: for each positive integer \(k\), the diagonal conjugation action of \(G\) on its \(k\)-fold Cartesian power has a comeager orbit.

Suppose \((Y,\mathscr F)\) is a uniformly locally finite coarse space. For an exponent \(r\) that is either zero or lies in the extended interval from \(1\) to \(\infty\), write \(\mathscr A_r(Y,\mathscr F)\) for the \(\ell^r\) uniform Roe algebra: the operator-norm closure of the algebra \(\mathscr D_r(Y,\mathscr F)\) consisting of controlled-propagation operators on \(\ell^r(Y)\). Call a norm-closed two-sided ideal \(J\subseteq\mathscr A_r(Y,\mathscr F)\) geometric when its controlled-propagation elements are norm dense in \(J\).

For finite exponents \(r,s>1\), the geometric-ideal lattices of \(\mathscr A_r(Y,\mathscr F)\) and \(\mathscr A_s(Y,\mathscr F)\) are isomorphic precisely when either the exponents coincide or
\[
s=\frac{r}{r-1}.
\]

Suppose \(H\) is a simple connected undirected graph with \(v\) vertices and \(e\) edges. If \(\theta\) is the second-largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of \(H\), then
\[
\theta \le \sqrt{\frac{2e-v-1}{2}}.
\]

Suppose \(\mathcal B\) is a \(W^\ast\)-bundle over a compact Hausdorff space \(K\) of zero covering dimension. Assume that there is a fixed type \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor \(N\) to which every fibre of \(\mathcal B\) is isomorphic. Show that \(\mathcal B\) admits a local trivialization around each point of \(K\).

Show that a complete, noncompact Riemannian manifold \((X,h)\) of dimension \(d\), with nonnegative Ricci curvature, is isometric to \(\mathbb{R}^{d}\) with its standard metric whenever it admits a locally bounded function
\[
v\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,d}(X)
\]
solving
\[
\operatorname{div}_{h}\!\left(\lvert\nabla^{h}v\rvert_{h}^{\,d-2}\nabla^{h}v\right)+\exp(v)=0
\]
in the weak sense. More precisely, require that every compactly supported test function \(\psi\in W_{0}^{1,d}(X)\) satisfy
\[
\int_X\left[
\lvert\nabla^{h}v\rvert_{h}^{\,d-2}
h(\nabla^{h}\psi,\nabla^{h}v)-\psi\,\exp(v)
\right]\,d\operatorname{vol}_{h}=0.
\]

Fix a positive prime \(\ell\) and a homomorphism \(\varphi:B\to C\) of commutative rings of characteristic \(\ell\). Write \(B^{(\mathrm{Fr})}\) for the ring \(B\) equipped with the \(B\)-algebra structure that sends each element to its \(\ell\)-th power. The relative Frobenius associated with \(\varphi\) is
\[
\Phi_\varphi:B^{(\mathrm{Fr})}\otimes_B C\longrightarrow C^{(\mathrm{Fr})},
\qquad
b\otimes c\longmapsto c^\ell\varphi(b).
\]

Call \(\varphi\) **b-nil formally unramified** when the following uniqueness property holds: whenever \(T\) is a ring of characteristic \(\ell\) and \(J\) is an ideal of \(T\) whose elements all have zero \(\ell\)-th power, each \(B\)-algebra map from \(C\) to \(T/J\) admits at most one lift to a \(B\)-algebra map from \(C\) to \(T\).

Prove that \(\varphi\) is formally unramified precisely when \(\Phi_\varphi\) is an epimorphism in the category of rings.

Suppose \(A\) is a commutative ring with unity. For each \(a\in A\), write
\[
I_a=\{\,b\in A:ab=0\,\}.
\]
Construct a graph \(H_A\) whose vertices are the nonzero zero-divisors of \(A\). Join distinct vertices \(a\) and \(c\) precisely when their annihilator ideals \(I_a\) and \(I_c\) are comparable under inclusion.

Prove that \(H_A\) is disconnected if and only if \(A\) is isomorphic to the direct product of two integral domains.
Suppose a group \(\Gamma\) has Kazhdan’s property (T) and is acylindrically hyperbolic. Prove that \(\Gamma\) has uniform exponential growth.

For a group \(H\), property \(R_{\infty}\) means that each automorphism \(\theta\) of \(H\) has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes, where \(u,v\in H\) belong to the same class precisely when
\[
v=t\,u\,\theta(t^{-1})
\]
for some \(t\in H\).

A closed manifold \(X\) is called Jiang-type when every continuous self-map \(h\colon X\to X\) satisfies the following conditions: if its Lefschetz number is nonzero, its Nielsen and Reidemeister numbers coincide; if its Lefschetz number vanishes, its Nielsen number also vanishes.

Show that a Jiang-type closed manifold \(X\) whose fundamental group has property \(R_{\infty}\) must be aspherical.

Let \(\mathcal P=\{1,\dots,m\}\) index the participants in a mixed-integer linear-quadratic generalized Nash game. Participant \(p\) chooses a vector \(y_p\) whose first \(r_p\) coordinates are nonnegative real numbers and whose remaining \(s_p\) coordinates are nonnegative integers. With the other participants’ choices fixed, participant \(p\) minimizes
\[
y_p^{\mathsf T}c_p+\sum_{q\in\mathcal P}y_p^{\mathsf T}H_{pq}^{\mathsf T}y_q
\]
under the componentwise restrictions
\[
B_{pp}y_p\;\ge\;h_p-\sum_{q\in\mathcal P\setminus\{p\}}B_{pq}y_q.
\]
Every entry of the matrices \(H_{pq},B_{pq}\) and vectors \(c_p,h_p\) is rational.

For this class of games, existence of a Nash equilibrium guarantees existence of an equilibrium with entirely rational coordinates if and only if every matrix \(H_{pp}\) is the zero matrix—that is, no participant’s objective contains a quadratic term involving only that participant’s own decision vector.

Prove that an irreducible Coxeter group \(G\) is finite if and only if it has the following property: for every nonnegative integer \(r\), there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of Bruhat intervals in \(G\) whose upper endpoint has Coxeter length exactly \(r\) greater than that of the lower endpoint.

There is an amenable unimodular random rooted network whose expected degree is finite, together with a finite-range operator \(T\) and a complex number \(z\), such that almost surely every eigenfunction of \(T\) with eigenvalue \(z\) has infinite support, while the corresponding eigenspace has strictly positive von Neumann dimension.

Fix a real parameter \(t\in(0,1)\). Write
\[
D_0(t)=1,\qquad D_n(t)=\prod_{r=1}^{n}(1-t^r)\quad(n\geq1),
\]
so that \(D_n(t)\) is the corresponding \(t\)-Pochhammer factor. On formal power series, define the normalized \(t\)-Borel operator \(T_t\) by
\[
T_t\!\left(\sum_{n\geq0}b_n w^n\right)
=\sum_{n\geq0}
\frac{n!\,b_n\,t^{\binom n2}(1-t)^n}{D_n(t)}\,w^n.
\]

Let \(\mathscr C\) be the classical Laguerre–Pólya class of real entire functions. Show that, for every such \(t\), the restriction \(T_t:\mathscr C\to\mathscr C\) is a bijection; in particular, its image is the whole class \(\mathscr C\).

Write \(\mathsf G(k,s)\) for the gamma law with shape \(k\) and scale \(s\), whose density on the positive half-line is
\[
f(w\mid k,s)=\frac{(w/s)^{k-1}e^{-w/s}}{s\,\Gamma(k)},\qquad w>0.
\]
Suppose \(a\) and \(c\) are fixed positive constants and \(\theta\) is an unknown positive scale. An observation \(U\) has distribution \(\mathsf G(a,\theta)\), and the independent quantity \(V\) to be predicted has distribution \(\mathsf G(ca,\theta)\).

When prediction is evaluated using Kullback–Leibler loss, the Bayesian predictive density of \(V\) given \(U\), obtained from Jeffreys’ prior with measure proportional to \(\theta^{-1}\,d\theta\), is admissible precisely when \(a\) exceeds \(1\).

Take lattice polytopes \(A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}\) and \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}\). Call a lattice polytope Ehrhart positive when its Ehrhart polynomial has no negative coefficients.

Inside \(\mathbb{R}^{m+n+1}\), define their join \(J(A,B)\) to be the convex hull of the two embedded copies
\[
\{0\}^{m}\times B\times\{0\}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
A\times\{0\}^{n}\times\{1\}.
\]
Whenever \(A\) and \(B\) are both Ehrhart positive, \(J(A,B)\) is Ehrhart positive as well.

Fix a prime \(\ell\) and an integer \(r\geq 1\), and let \(C\) be a cyclic group with \(\ell^{\,r}\) elements. Choose a subgroup \(K\leq \operatorname{Aut}(C)\), and form the orbit Schur ring whose basic sets are the \(K\)-orbits on \(C\). Show that the Terwilliger algebra of the associated association scheme is almost commutative precisely when \(K\) consists only of the identity automorphism or is the full automorphism group of \(C\).

Fix an exponent \(q\in(1,\infty)\). For each integer \(n\ge 2\) and coordinate index \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define a discrete Riesz transform \(T_{n,j}\) on \(\ell^q(\mathbb Z^n)\) by convolution with the kernel
\[
H_{n,j}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \pi^{-(n+1)/2}\Gamma\!\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)x_j\,|x|^{-(n+1)},&x\ne 0,\\[4pt]
0,&x=0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(|x|\) denotes the Euclidean length of \(x\).

Show that there is a positive constant \(M_q\), depending only on \(q\), for which
\[
\sup_{n\ge 2}\ \max_{1\le j\le n}
\|T_{n,j}\|_{\ell^q(\mathbb Z^n)\to\ell^q(\mathbb Z^n)}
\le M_q.
\]

Fix an integer \(m\geq 2\), and let \(B\) be an \(m\)-dimensional fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index \(h\in(1/4,1/2]\). Work on the canonical path space
\[
\mathcal W=C_0([0,1];\mathbb R^m),
\]
consisting of continuous paths that start at the origin, equipped with its Borel \(\sigma\)-field and the Gaussian law of \(B\). Put \(N=\lfloor h^{-1}\rfloor\), and choose a Hölder exponent \(\beta\) satisfying
\[
0<\beta<h,\qquad \beta^{-1}<N+1.
\]

Consider random geometric rough paths
\[
\mathbf B:\mathcal W\longrightarrow
C^{\beta\text{-Höl}}\bigl([0,1];\mathcal G^N(\mathbb R^m)\bigr)
\]
whose first level agrees with \(B\). Call such a lift local when, for every interval \([a,b]\subseteq[0,1]\), every order \(k\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), and every choice of coordinate labels \(j_1,\ldots,j_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the coefficient \(\mathbf B_{a,b}^{j_1\cdots j_k}\) is measurable with respect to
\[
\sigma\!\left(
B_v^j-B_a^j:\ a\leq v\leq b,\ 
j\in\{j_1,\ldots,j_k\}
\right).
\]
Require also that every component of the lift be square-integrable.

Restrict attention to these local, square-integrable lifts whose laws have all of the following symmetries:

- Relabelling coordinates leaves the law unchanged: for every permutation \(\pi\) of the \(m\) coordinates,
  \[
  \mathcal L(\pi_*\mathbf B)=\mathcal L(\mathbf B).
  \]
- Increments are stationary: whenever \(a,r\geq0\) and \(a+r\leq1\),
  \[
  \mathcal L(\mathbf B_{a,a+r})=\mathcal L(\mathbf B_{0,r}).
  \]
- Each level has the fractional Brownian scaling law: for the same \(a,r\) and each \(1\leq k\leq N\),
  \[
  \mathcal L\!\left(\mathbf B_{a,a+r}^{(k)}\right)
  =
  \mathcal L\!\left(r^{kh}\mathbf B_{0,1}^{(k)}\right).
  \]

For every Hurst index in the stated range, the canonical rough path lift is the unique lift satisfying all these requirements.
Prove that every finite group \(H\) has a nilpotent subgroup \(N\) whose order is at least the number of conjugacy classes of \(H\).

Suppose coupons come in \(m\) varieties, where \(m\) is an integer at least two, and successive draws are independent with type probabilities \(\boldsymbol{q}=(q_a)_{a=1}^{m}\). Collectors are arranged in a line. Each drawn coupon goes to the first collector, who keeps it if that variety is new to them and otherwise forwards it to the next collector. Every subsequent collector follows the same rule.

Stop drawing when the first collector has obtained every variety. For an integer \(r\) at least two, write \(D_r^{(m)}(\boldsymbol{q})\) for the number of varieties absent from the \(r\)-th collector’s collection at that moment.

Show that the map
\[
\boldsymbol{q}\longmapsto \mathbb{E}\!\left[D_r^{(m)}(\boldsymbol{q})\right]
\]
is Schur-concave on the probability simplex. Consequently, establish that its maximum is attained when every coupon variety has probability \(m^{-1}\).

Given a graph \(Q\), call a graph \(X\) \(Q\)-saturated if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to \(Q\), yet inserting any missing edge creates such a subgraph. Write \(\sigma_Q(t)\) for the smallest number of edges among all \(Q\)-saturated graphs with \(t\) vertices. For a graph \(R\), let \(U(R)\) be obtained by adjoining one new vertex adjacent to every vertex of \(R\).

Fix an integer \(q\geq 4\). Form \(R\) by deleting one edge from a complete graph on \(q-1\) vertices and then taking its disjoint union with an isolated vertex. Show that, for all sufficiently large integers \(N\),
\[
\sigma_{U(R)}(N)=\sigma_R(N-1)+(N-1).
\]

Consider a convex polygon \(Q\) with \(2m\) cyclically ordered vertices \(V_1,\ldots,V_{2m}\), with subscripts interpreted modulo \(2m\). Assume that each side is parallel to the side \(m\) positions farther along the boundary, and that consecutive directed side vectors have positive scalar product; explicitly,
\[
(V_{j+2}-V_{j+1})\cdot(V_{j+1}-V_j)>0
\qquad\text{for every }j.
\]

Write \(p\) for the perimeter of \(Q\) and \(B\) for its enclosed area. Define midpoint vertices \(M_j\) by
\[
2M_j=V_j+V_{j+m}.
\]
These vertices, in their indexed order, form the Wigner caustic of \(Q\). Let its signed area be \(S\), with the convention
\[
2S=\sum_{j=1}^{2m}\det(M_j,M_{j+1}).
\]

Prove that
\[
B+2|S|\le \frac{p^2}{8m}\cot\!\left(\frac{\pi}{2m}\right),
\]
and that equality occurs precisely when \(Q\) is a regular polygon with \(2m\) sides.

Fix a positive integer \(n\). Equip the set of affine lines in Euclidean \(n\)-space with the quotient topology induced by the map sending an ordered pair of distinct points to the unique line through them.

Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be a finite collection containing at least two open convex subsets of this space, with any two members disjoint. A line is a transversal of \(\mathcal{C}\) if it meets every member. Prove that each connected component of the set of these transversals, given the subspace topology, has vanishing reduced homology in every degree.

Fix an integer \(k\ge 3\). For all sufficiently large integers \(m\), let \(\mathcal A\) be a family of subsets of an \(m\)-element set, each containing exactly \(k+1\) elements. If the VC-dimension of \(\mathcal A\) is exactly \(k\), then
\[
|\mathcal A|\le \binom{m-4}{k-2}+\binom{m-1}{k}.
\]

There is a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers \((b_k)_{k\ge 1}\) satisfying
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{k}{b_k}=0
\]
for which the series
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{b_k}{2^{b_k}}
\]
converges to a positive rational number \(q\).

Let \(D\) be an integral domain, with unit group \(D^\times\). A nonzero nonunit \(p\) is called an **irreducible**, or **atom**, when every decomposition \(uv=p\) has at least one unit among \(u\) and \(v\). Call an element **atomic** if it is either a unit or a finite product of irreducibles; call \(D\) **atomic** if all its nonzero elements are atomic.

Consider the following additional notions:
- \(D\) is a **finite factorization domain (FFD)** if each nonzero nonunit admits a positive finite number of factorizations into irreducibles, identifying factorizations that differ only by rearrangement or replacement of factors by associates.
- \(D\) has the **irreducible divisor finite (IDF) property** if, for each nonzero element, its irreducible divisors represent only finitely many associate classes.
- \(D\) is **almost atomic** if every nonzero \(x\in D\) admits an atomic multiplier \(y\in D\) for which \(yx\) is atomic.
- \(D\) is **nearly atomic** if some nonzero \(c\in D\) has the property that every nonzero member of the principal ideal generated by \(c\) is atomic as an element of \(D\).

Prove that \(D\) is a finite factorization domain exactly when it is both almost atomic and IDF.

Fix a positive integer \(d\), a number \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and an exponent \(q>1\). Suppose that the weight parameter \(\beta\) satisfies
\[
\beta\ge 0,\qquad \beta<d,\qquad \beta<2\alpha,\qquad \beta<2\alpha(q-1).
\]
Choose a nonnegative, nonzero function \(\phi\) belonging to both \(L^\infty(\mathbb R^d)\) and \(L^1(\mathbb R^d)\).

Define the fractional Laplacian \(\mathcal A_\alpha\) by
\[
(\mathcal A_\alpha h)(z)
=
\frac{4^\alpha\Gamma(d/2+\alpha)}
{\pi^{d/2}|\Gamma(-\alpha)|}
\,\operatorname{P.V.}\!\int_{\mathbb R^d}
\bigl(h(z)-h(w)\bigr)|z-w|^{-d-2\alpha}\,dw.
\]
For an amplitude \(\delta>0\), let \(S_\delta\in(0,+\infty]\) be the lifespan of mild solutions of
\[
\partial_\tau v(\tau,z)
=
|z|^{-\beta}|v(\tau,z)|^q-\mathcal A_\alpha v(\tau,z),
\qquad z\in\mathbb R^d,\quad \tau>0,
\]
subject to
\[
v(0,z)=\delta\,\phi(z).
\]
Set
\[
q_{\mathrm c}=\frac{d+2\alpha-\beta}{d}.
\]
Then there is a number \(\delta_*>0\) such that every amplitude \(\delta\in(0,\delta_*)\) yields finite lifespan when \(1<q<q_{\mathrm c}\), whereas \(S_\delta=+\infty\) whenever \(q\ge q_{\mathrm c}\).

Consider a connected bipartite graph drawn on a closed orientable surface as a dessin d’enfant. Its passport records, in order, the degrees of its black vertices, white vertices, and faces as three partitions of its total number of edges. Call the passport uniform when, within each partition, all parts have the same size.

Show that every uniform passport of genus at least two can be realized by a dessin d’enfant whose only automorphism is the identity.

Consider a collection of \(m\) distinct coupons, where \(m\) and \(r\) are positive integers satisfying \(1\le r\le m\). Each trial independently produces a set of exactly \(r\) coupons.

A sampling rule chooses uniformly from a fixed family \(\mathscr F\) of such sets. Call the rule balanced when each coupon belongs to equally many members of \(\mathscr F\). Write \(E_{\mathscr F}(m,r)\) for the mean number of trials required until every coupon has appeared at least once. Let \(E_{\mathrm{all}}(m,r)\) denote the corresponding mean when the family consists of every \(r\)-element subset of the collection.

For every admissible pair \(m,r\) and every balanced family \(\mathscr F\), the following bound holds:
\[
E_{\mathrm{all}}(m,r)\ge E_{\mathscr F}(m,r).
\]

Consider a positive-definite quadratic form \(C\) on the space of symmetric second-order tensors over the Euclidean plane, interpreted as an elasticity stiffness tensor. Given a planar vector \(v\), define its Christoffel matrix \(G_C(v)\) by
\[
[G_C(v)]_{rs}=\sum_{p,q=1}^{2}v_p\,C_{rpqs}\,v_q,
\qquad r,s\in\{1,2\}.
\]
The associated slowness curve is
\[
S_C=\bigl\{v\in\mathbb R^2:\det\!\bigl(I_2-G_C(v)\bigr)=0\bigr\},
\]
where \(I_2\) denotes the two-dimensional identity matrix.

The possible singularities of such planar slowness curves are exactly ordinary cusps, ordinary nodes—transverse self-crossings—and ordinary tacnodes, arising from tangency between a circle and an ellipse with the same center.

Suppose \(S\) is a simple first-order theory containing two definable equivalence relations \(R\) and \(Q\). Assume that each relation has the non-finite cover property (NFCP) and is stable. Show that the relational composition of \(R\) with \(Q\) is stable.

For a graph \(H\) whose number of edges is divisible by an integer \(m\ge 2\), define \(\rho_m(H)\) to be the smallest integer \(N\) with the following property: whenever the edges of the complete graph on \(N\) vertices are assigned elements of \(\mathbb Z_m\), some subgraph isomorphic to \(H\) has edge labels adding to the identity of \(\mathbb Z_m\).

Write \(B(a,b)\) for the complete bipartite graph with part sizes \(a\) and \(b\). For integers \(a\ge 2\) and \(r\ge 1\), the zero-sum Ramsey number is
\[
\rho_3\bigl(B(a,3r)\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
3r+a+1, & \text{if }a=2,\text{ or if }r=1\text{ and }3\le a\le 7,\\
3r+a, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Equip \(\mathbb{R}^{3}\), with coordinates \((t,u,v)\), with the Lorentzian metric
\[
g=du^{2}+dv^{2}-dt^{2},
\]
and denote this space by \(\mathbb{E}^{3}_{1}\).

For an open Riemann surface \(N\), call a smooth map \(F:N\to\mathbb{E}^{3}_{1}\) a **maxface** when its differential is nonzero at every point and there is a dense open set \(U\subset N\) on which \(F\) is a spacelike immersion whose mean curvature vanishes everywhere. Write
\[
\Sigma_F=\{p\in N:(F^{*}g)_p\text{ is degenerate}\}
\]
for its singular locus.

Prove that, for every such surface \(N\) and every maxface \(F\), the set \(F(\Sigma_F)\) is nowhere dense in \(\mathbb{E}^{3}_{1}\).

Suppose \(C\) is a finite skew brace with additive law \(\oplus\) and multiplicative law \(\odot\). For each \(x\in C\), define the map \(L_x:C\to C\) by the identity
\[
x\oplus L_x(y)=x\odot y \qquad (y\in C).
\]
An additive subgroup stable under every \(L_x\) is called a left ideal. A subset that forms a subgroup under each of the two laws is called a sub-skew brace.

Fix a prime \(\ell\), and let \(m\) be the largest integer for which \(\ell^m\) divides the cardinality of \(C\). A sub-skew brace with exactly \(\ell^m\) elements is called a Sylow \(\ell\)-sub-skew brace.

Show that any sub-skew brace of \(C\) whose cardinality is a power of \(\ell\) lies inside a Sylow \(\ell\)-sub-skew brace of \(C\).

Write \(Q\) for the path with four vertices. For integers \(N\) and \(M\), define \(r(N,M;Q)\) as follows: among all graphs with \(N\) vertices and \(M\) edges, and all edge-colorings of those graphs in which the three edges of every copy of \(Q\) receive pairwise different colors, take the smallest number of colors used.

Prove that for each real \(\delta>0\), there is a constant \(a_\delta>0\) such that, whenever \(N\) is sufficiently large,
\[
a_\delta N^2
<
r\!\left(
N,\,
\frac{N(N-1)}{2}
-\left\lfloor\frac{N^2}{N^\delta}\right\rfloor
;\,Q
\right).
\]

Call a closed manifold virtually fibred over the circle when some finite-sheeted covering space of it is the total space of a fibre bundle over the circle. Suppose that \(X\) is a closed aspherical manifold of dimension \(n\), where \(n\) is at least three. Assume that, over each field, every \(L^{2}\)-Betti number of \(X\) is zero, and that its fundamental group is residually torsion-free nilpotent. Then \(X\) is virtually fibred over the circle.

Let the spatial dimension be an integer \(n>1\). Consider an incompressible fluid governed by the one-phase Navier–Stokes free-boundary equations with surface tension, whose initial region is the exterior of a bubble in Euclidean \(n\)-space. The joint regularizing action of viscosity and surface tension rules out finite-time splash singularities. More precisely, if the bubble collapses through self-intersection of its free boundary at a finite time \(T_*\), then the supremum of the principal curvatures of that boundary must blow up as time approaches \(T_*\) from below.

Let \(n\ge 3\) be an integer and let \(a>0\). Consider the equation
\[
\Delta v(y)+\|y\|^{a}\,v(y)^{\,1+\frac{2(a+2)}{n-2}}=0,
\qquad y\in\mathbb R^{n}.
\]
There exists a positive, nonradial classical solution whose decay satisfies
\[
v(y)=O\!\left(\frac{1}{\|y\|^{n-2}}\right)
\quad\text{as }\|y\|\to\infty
\]
if and only if \(a+2=2m\) for some integer \(m\ge 1\).
